summary: Independent review of all 82 original targets, with one added admissible external-tensor theorem. The corrected 83-node packet plans classical and solid locally analytic representations, induction, Orlik–Strauch and Jacquet constructions, and Ding’s local GL_n extension maps. It remains partial with explicit proof and supplier contracts; no formalisation or gap-free closure is claimed.

nodes.title: Rational points of a smooth affine group are a locally analytic group
nodes.statement: Let L/ℚ_p be finite and 𝐆 a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over L. Then G = 𝐆(L), with the topology of ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.0, carries the canonical structure of locally L-analytic group (a Lie group over L in the sense of Schneider, §13; in Mathlib, a LieGroup modelled on L^d with analytic smoothness) induced by the algebraic charts, with its usual topology. For every closed immersion 𝐆 ↪ GL_N it is a closed analytic submanifold of the open subset GL_N(L) ⊂ M_N(L), its tangent space at 1 is Lie(𝐆) ⊂ gl_N(L) with the commutator bracket, and the closed subgroups P(L), M_P(L), N_P(L), T(L) attached to a parabolic P = M_P N_P and a maximal torus T are locally analytic subgroups with Lie algebras p, m_P, n_P, t. Restricting scalars along ℚ_p ⊆ L makes G a locally ℚ_p-analytic group of dimension [L:ℚ_p]·dim 𝐆 whose ℚ_p-Lie algebra is g viewed over ℚ_p. If E/ℚ_p contains the images of all embeddings σ : L → E (the set Σ_L, of cardinality d_L = [L:ℚ_p]) then L ⊗_{ℚ_p} E ≅ ∏_{σ∈Σ_L} E, x ⊗ y ↦ (σ(x)y)_σ, and hence g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E ≅ ∏_σ g_σ with g_σ := g ⊗_{L,σ} E, and U(g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E) ≅ ⊗_σ U(g_σ).
hypotheses: L/ℚ_p finite; 𝐆 smooth affine over L (reductive from LR.4 on).
Canonical means compatible with regular and étale algebraic charts; the topology and group law alone do not determine an L-analytic atlas.
proofSteps: In a neighbourhood of each rational point of a smooth closed affine subgroup of GL_N, choose N² − d defining equations with independent differentials and a Zariski neighbourhood on which their zero locus agrees with the subgroup. Apply the analytic inverse function theorem (SCHN11 Proposition 6.4, pp. 42–43) to the equations together with complementary coordinates. Corollary 4.5, p. 24, alone provides topological charts and is insufficient for analyticity.

Multiplication and inversion are restrictions of the analytic operations of GL_N(L), so 𝐆(L) is a Lie group over L; its tangent space at 1 is the kernel of the Jacobian, i.e. Lie(𝐆)(L) (ReductiveGroups Layer 2), with the commutator bracket (SCHN11 §14).

Regular transition maps between these algebraic local charts are L-analytic. This proves independence of the immersion and uniqueness among atlases compatible with the algebraic charts; no uniqueness claim for arbitrary topologically compatible L-analytic group structures is used.

Restriction of scalars: an L-analytic chart L^d ⊃ U is a ℚ_p-analytic chart of ℚ_p^{d·d_L}; the decomposition of L ⊗_{ℚ_p} E is the Chinese remainder theorem for the separable extension L/ℚ_p split by E.
acceptance: For 𝐆 = GL_n the analytic structure is that of the open subset GL_n(L) ⊂ M_n(L) and g = gl_n(L).
For L ≠ ℚ_p and 𝐆 = 𝔾_m, G = L^× has dimension 1 over L and d_L over ℚ_p, and Lie(G) ⊗_{ℚ_p} E ≅ E^{Σ_L}.

For a nontrivial automorphism σ of a finite Galois extension L/ℚ_p, transporting the additive atlas by σ preserves the topological group but changes its L-analytic structure. The canonical statement therefore requires algebraic compatibility.

sources.match: GL_n(K) is a Lie group as the open submanifold det ≠ 0 of K^{n²}; Lie groups have a well-defined dimension.
An implicit-function statement: a strictly differentiable map with surjective derivative has zero set locally a graph, which gives the submanifold charts used for 𝐆(L) ⊂ GL_N(L).
For nonarchimedean K, gl_n(K) is the Lie algebra of GL_n(K).
States the decomposition L ⊗_{ℚ_p} E ≅ ∏_σ E and deduces g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E ≅ ∏_σ g_σ and U(g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E) ≅ ⊗_σ U(g_σ) for the ℚ_p-Lie algebra of G(L).
The analytic inverse function theorem upgrades the local smooth algebraic coordinate presentation to analytic submanifold charts.

nodes.title: Locally analytic representations
nodes.statement: Let F ∈ {ℚ_p, L} be the field of analyticity, G a locally F-analytic group (LR.0/rational-points-analytic-group, by restriction of scalars when F = ℚ_p), and E ⊇ F a complete, spherically complete nonarchimedean field (a finite extension of ℚ_p in every application). A locally F-analytic representation of G over E is a barrelled Hausdorff locally convex E-vector space V with an action of G by continuous E-linear maps such that for every v ∈ V the orbit map ρ_v : G → V, g ↦ g·v, is a locally F-analytic V-valued function (an element of C^{F-an}(G, V), LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0). Morphisms are continuous G-equivariant E-linear maps; this gives the category Rep^{la}_E(G) (Rep^{F-la}_E(G) when F must be named). V is of compact type, LB or Banach when its underlying space is. Unqualified 'locally analytic' means locally ℚ_p-analytic, the convention of Ding, of Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen and of Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni; 'locally L-analytic' (Schneider–Teitelbaum, Orlik–Strauch) is the case F = L.
hypotheses: Barrelledness makes the action map G × V → V continuous (Banach–Steinhaus), so the topology and the action interact as for Banach representations.
For F = L, E must contain L; for F = ℚ_p no condition on E beyond ℚ_p ⊆ E.
proofSteps: Locally analytic V-valued functions on a locally F-analytic manifold are those that are, on a cover by charts, sums of convergent power series with coefficients in BH-subspaces of V (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0/locally-analytic-function-space); the definition only asks this of orbit maps.

Continuity of G × V → V: each g acts continuously and the orbit maps are continuous; for barrelled V the equicontinuity of {g : g ∈ K} for compact K follows from the Banach–Steinhaus theorem (L0/barrelled-banach-steinhaus), as in ST02 §3.
acceptance: Every finite-dimensional algebraic representation of 𝐆 over E, restricted to G = 𝐆(L), is locally L-analytic (orbit maps are polynomial in matrix entries).

nodes.title: The derived action of the Lie algebra
nodes.statement: Let V be a locally F-analytic representation of G with F-Lie algebra g. For x ∈ g and v ∈ V put x·v := (d/dt)(exp(tx)·v)|_{t=0}, using the exponential of G near 1 (SCHN11 §18) and the analyticity of the orbit map. Then x ↦ (v ↦ x·v) is an F-linear Lie algebra homomorphism g → End_cont(V), which extends to an E-algebra homomorphism U(g ⊗_F E) → End_cont(V). It satisfies g(x·v) = (Ad(g)x)·(g·v) for g ∈ G, commutes with every morphism of locally analytic representations, and coincides with the action of the distributions x̃ ∈ D(G, E) of LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.1/lie-algebra-in-distributions under the module structure of LR.0/distribution-module-structure. For F = ℚ_p and E splitting L, U(g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E) = ⊗_σ U(g_σ) acts, so V decomposes its Lie action into components indexed by Σ_L. On spaces of functions the convention is (x·f)(g) = (d/dt) f(exp(−tx)g)|_{t=0} for the left regular action, as in Breuil.
hypotheses: The exponential is defined on a neighbourhood of 0 in g; only the germ at t = 0 enters.
proofSteps: Differentiate the analytic orbit maps. For fixed x, the difference quotients are pointwise bounded continuous linear operators on the barrelled space V; Banach–Steinhaus gives equicontinuity and continuity of their pointwise limit (ST02 §3, pp. 12–13).

Differentiate the group commutator identity in two variables to obtain the Lie bracket relation; differentiate conjugation to obtain Ad-equivariance. These steps use the analytic group charts, before any distribution-module construction. Apply UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.lift to extend the action.

After LR.0/distribution-module-structure is constructed, its scalar integration formula identifies the distribution x̃ acting on v with the same orbit derivative. This is a later compatibility result, not an input to the construction.
acceptance: On a finite-dimensional algebraic representation the derived action is the differential of the algebraic action (ReductiveGroups Layer 2).

nodes.title: The distribution algebra of a locally analytic group
nodes.statement: Let G be a locally F-analytic group (not necessarily compact) and H ⊆ G a compact open subgroup. C^{F-an}(G, E) = ∏_{gH ∈ G/H} C^{F-an}(gH, E) as locally convex spaces, and D(G, E) := C^{F-an}(G, E)′_b is the locally convex direct sum ⊕_{gH∈G/H} δ_g ∗ D(H, E), where D(H, E) is the Fréchet algebra of LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.1/distribution-algebra. Convolution λ ∗ μ = m_*(λ ⊗̂ μ) makes D(G, E) an associative unital E-algebra with unit δ_1 and separately continuous multiplication; δ_g ∗ δ_h = δ_{gh}; E[G] → D(G, E) is injective with dense image; for open H′ ⊆ G, D(H′, E) is a subalgebra and D(G, E) is free as a right D(H′, E)-module with summands δ_g D(H′, E) indexed by gH′, and free as a left module with summands D(H′, E)δ_g indexed by H′g; U(g ⊗_F E) ⊂ D(H, E) ⊂ D(G, E); and g ↦ g⁻¹ induces an anti-involution, so left modules suffice. For F = ℚ_p and L ≠ ℚ_p the closed embedding C^{L-an} ⊂ C^{ℚ_p-an} dualises to a surjection D_{ℚ_p}(G, E) ↠ D_L(G, E). Unless stated otherwise D(G, E) is the ℚ_p-analytic algebra.
hypotheses: E spherically complete, so that strong duals behave as in LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0.
Separate continuity only: for noncompact G the multiplication on the direct sum is not jointly continuous in general, and nothing below uses joint continuity.

Convolution is defined coset by coset from ND.1/distribution-algebra and m_* (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0/locally-analytic-pullback); associativity and the unit follow from the compact case and δ_g ∗ δ_h = δ_{gh} (ST02 Proposition 2.3).
Density of E[G] and freeness over D(H′, E) reduce to ND.1/open-subgroup-decomposition for the compact pieces.

nodes.title: Locally analytic representations are D(G, E)-modules
nodes.statement: Let V be a locally F-analytic representation of G over E. There is a unique separately continuous bilinear map D(G, E) × V → V, (μ, v) ↦ μ ∗ v, making V a left D(G, E)-module, with δ_g ∗ v = g·v, extending the derived action of U(g ⊗_F E) (LR.0/derived-lie-action), and characterised by λ(μ ∗ v) = μ(g ↦ λ(g·v)) for all λ ∈ V′. For fixed v the map D(G, E) → V, μ ↦ μ ∗ v, is continuous (the integration map of the orbit). Every continuous G-equivariant linear map between locally analytic representations is D(G, E)-linear.
hypotheses: V barrelled (part of the definition of a locally analytic representation).
proofSteps: For fixed v and a compact chart meeting the support of μ, factor the analytic orbit map through a Banach (BH) subspace of V. Integrate its convergent power series there against the restricted distribution and sum over the finitely many supporting charts. ST02 §2–3, pp. 8, 12–13, proves independence of the choices. This does not assume a global identity C^an(G,V) = C^an(G,E) ⊗̂ V for arbitrary barrelled V.
Separate continuity in μ is continuity of the integration map; in v it follows from barrelledness and Banach–Steinhaus.
δ_g ∗ v = g·v by evaluation; the module axioms hold on Dirac distributions and extend by density of E[G] (LR.0/distribution-algebra).
The formula λ(μ ∗ v) = μ(λ ∘ ρ_v) holds by construction; uniqueness follows from Hahn–Banach (L0/nonarchimedean-hahn-banach). G-maps commute with Dirac distributions, hence with all of D(G, E).
acceptance: For V = C^an(G, E) with left translation, μ ∗ f is the convolution of μ with f (ST02 §3).

sources.match: The map (μ, v) ↦ μ ∗ v is separately continuous, V is a D(G, K)-module extending the U(g)-action, and continuous G-maps are D(G, K)-linear.
Uses the continuity of μ ↦ μ ∗ w from D(G) to W and the integration formula λ(μ ∗ w) = ∫ λ(g·w) dμ(g) for λ ∈ W*.

nodes.title: Schneider–Teitelbaum duality for representations of compact type
nodes.statement: The functor V ↦ V′_b is an anti-equivalence between locally F-analytic representations of G on E-vector spaces of compact type, with continuous G-maps, and separately continuous D(G, E)-modules whose underlying space is a nuclear Fréchet space, with continuous D(G, E)-linear maps. The D(G, E)-module structure on V′_b is the contragredient of LR.0/distribution-module-structure, composed with the anti-involution g ↦ g⁻¹.
hypotheses: E spherically complete, so that compact-type and nuclear Fréchet spaces are reflexive and in duality (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0/compact-type-nuclear-duality).
proofSteps: Compact-type spaces and nuclear Fréchet spaces are anti-equivalent under the strong dual (L0/compact-type-nuclear-duality).
A locally analytic structure on V gives a separately continuous D(G, E)-module structure on V′_b by transposition (LR.0/distribution-module-structure).

Conversely a separately continuous D(G, E)-module structure on a nuclear Fréchet M gives a G-action on M′_b by restriction to Dirac distributions, and the orbit maps are locally analytic by the reflexivity argument of ST02 Corollary 3.3.
acceptance: For G compact and V = C^an(G, E), the dual is D(G, E) itself, free of rank one.

nodes.title: Continuity of matrix-coefficient maps
nodes.statement: Let W be a locally F-analytic representation of G on an E-space of compact type and λ ∈ W′. Then the map F_λ : W → C^{F-an}(G, E), w ↦ (g ↦ λ(g·w)), is well defined, G-equivariant for the right regular action, and continuous.
hypotheses: W of compact type, hence reflexive.
proofSteps: F_λ(w) is locally analytic because it is λ composed with the orbit map ρ_w.

For compact open H ⊆ G, C^an(H,E) is of compact type and reflexive, so transposition and the separately continuous dual distribution action prove continuity of W → C^an(gH,E). Taking the product over G/H gives continuity into C^an(G,E). The full function space need not be of compact type or reflexive when G is noncompact.
Equivariance is the identity λ(gh·w) = (F_λ(h·w))(g).
acceptance: For W = C^an(G, E) and λ = evaluation at 1, F_λ is the identity of C^an(G, E) (up to the inversion convention).

sources.match: For a locally analytic representation W of compact type and a continuous linear form λ, the matrix-coefficient map W → LA(G) is continuous; the proof uses reflexivity and the continuity of μ ↦ μ ∗ w.

nodes.title: Weakly null sequences are null over a spherically complete field
nodes.statement: Let E be spherically complete and V a Hausdorff locally convex E-vector space. A sequence (v_n) in V converges to 0 if and only if λ(v_n) → 0 for every λ ∈ V′.
hypotheses: Spherical completeness of E is essential: it gives the Hahn–Banach theorem (L0/nonarchimedean-hahn-banach), on which the argument rests.
proofSteps: Strong convergence implies weak convergence.
Conversely, reduce to the seminormed quotients V_q := V/ker q for the continuous seminorms q; weak convergence passes to V_q because continuous forms on V_q are continuous forms on V.

The remaining nonarchimedean Schur step is exactly the open proof contract: weak nullness in each seminormed quotient implies convergence in its norm over a spherically complete field. DLB17 Lemme 5.10, p. 29, states this without proof. Neither weak compactness of the sequence together with 0 nor the listed compactoid supplier alone supplies that implication. The node records the sourced statement, not a completed compactoid proof.
acceptance: In c_0(ℕ, E) the unit vectors e_n do not tend to 0 weakly (pair with the bounded sequence (1, 1, …) ∈ ℓ^∞ = c_0′), consistently with ‖e_n‖ = 1.

sources.match: Asserts, without proof, that in a locally convex space over a spherically complete field a sequence tends to 0 if and only if it tends weakly to 0.

nodes.title: Completed external tensor products of representations
nodes.statement: Let V_i be a locally F-analytic representation of G_i on a space of compact type, i = 1, 2. The completed tensor product V_1 ⊗̂_E V_2 (projective and inductive completed tensor products agree for these spaces) is of compact type and is a locally analytic representation of G_1 × G_2 with (g_1, g_2)(v_1 ⊗ v_2) = g_1v_1 ⊗ g_2v_2. Its strong dual is V_1′_b ⊗̂_E V_2′_b as a module over D(G_1 × G_2, E) ⊇ D(G_1, E) ⊗_E D(G_2, E) (for compact opens, D(H_1 × H_2, E) = D(H_1, E) ⊗̂_E D(H_2, E)). Admissibility of the external product is the later LR.1/admissible-external-tensor theorem; restriction along the diagonal G → G × G gives the internal completed tensor product, in particular the twist V ⊗ χ by a locally analytic character χ.
hypotheses: Both spaces are of compact type. Exactness below concerns strict short exact sequences of compact-type spaces. No assertion for arbitrary semi-complete LB representations is made.
proofSteps: Completed tensor products of compact-type spaces are of compact type and dual to the completed tensor products of the nuclear Fréchet duals (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0/compact-type-tensor-products).

Use the compact-type Banach presentations and Emerton Proposition 3.6.18, p. 74 (via Propositions 3.5.15 and 3.6.12): completed tensor products of analytic vectors have analytic orbit maps for the product group. Density of elementary tensors alone does not prove this, since analytic vectors need not be closed.

Strict exactness and strong-dual compatibility are supplied by the compact-type tensor-product and nuclear-duality theorems. Admissibility is proved only after admissibility has been defined in LR.1/admissible-external-tensor.
acceptance: For G_2 = 1 and V_2 = E, V_1 ⊗̂ E = V_1.

nodes.title: Coadmissible modules over the distribution algebra of a p-adic group
nodes.statement: Let G be a locally F-analytic group. A left D(G, E)-module M is coadmissible if, for one (equivalently every) compact open subgroup H ⊆ G, its restriction to D(H, E) is a coadmissible module over the Fréchet–Stein algebra D(H, E) (LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.2/coadmissible-module, ND.2/frechet-stein-distribution). It then carries the canonical Fréchet topology of the D(H, E)-module, independent of H, for which D(G, E) acts separately continuously. 𝒞_G denotes the full subcategory of Mod(D(G, E)) of coadmissible modules.
hypotheses: Independence of H: for H ⊆ H′ compact open, D(H′, E) is finite free over D(H, E), so a D(H′, E)-module is coadmissible iff it is coadmissible over D(H, E) (ST03 Lemma 3.8, via ND.2/coadmissible-theorems).
proofSteps: Apply ND.2/coadmissible-theorems (the last statement, coadmissibility along a continuous map of Fréchet–Stein algebras with coadmissible target) to D(H, E) → D(H′, E).
The canonical topology does not depend on H because D(H ∩ H′, E)-linear maps between coadmissible modules are continuous and strict (ND.2/coadmissible-theorems).
acceptance: For G compact, 𝒞_G is the category of coadmissible D(G, E)-modules of ND.2.

uses.how: the essential image of the dual of admissible representations
V^∨ is coadmissible over D(H, E) for any compact open H ⊆ GL_n(K)
Schneider–Teitelbaum's Lemma 3.6 on submodules of coadmissible modules

nodes.title: Admissible locally analytic representations
nodes.statement: A locally F-analytic representation V of G over E is admissible if V is of compact type and its strong dual V′_b, with the module structure of LR.0/compact-type-duality, is a coadmissible D(G, E)-module whose canonical topology is the strong topology (equivalently, V is admissible as a representation of one, or every, compact open subgroup). It is strongly admissible if moreover V′ is finitely generated over D(H, E) for a compact open H (Emerton). Rep^a_E(G) denotes the full subcategory of admissible representations.
hypotheses: Compact type is part of the definition; for compact-type spaces Emerton's and Schneider–Teitelbaum's admissibility agree.
proofSteps: Independence of the compact open subgroup is LR.1/coadmissible-module.
A coadmissible module carries a unique Fréchet topology for which the action is continuous (ND.2/coadmissible-theorems), so 'with the strong topology' is a condition only on V, not extra data.
acceptance: C^{F-an}(H, E) for compact H with left translation is admissible: its dual D(H, E) is free of rank one.

nodes.title: Schneider–Teitelbaum anti-equivalence
nodes.statement: The functor V ↦ V′_b is an anti-equivalence between Rep^a_E(G) and the category 𝒞_G of coadmissible D(G, E)-modules (with all D(G, E)-linear maps, which are automatically continuous for the canonical topologies).
proofSteps: LR.0/compact-type-duality is an anti-equivalence onto separately continuous D(G, E)-modules on nuclear Fréchet spaces.

For D(H,E), the canonical Fréchet topology of a coadmissible module is nuclear by ST03 Lemma 6.1, pp. 31–32, using the compact transition maps of the distribution-algebra presentation. Its action is separately continuous, and module maps are continuous. Restricting to compact opens gives the noncompact statement. Nuclearity is specific to distribution algebras here, not to arbitrary Fréchet–Stein algebras.
acceptance: Under the anti-equivalence, the trivial representation corresponds to E with augmentation action, and C^an(H, E) to D(H, E).

sources.match: The functor from admissible representations to coadmissible modules, V ↦ V′, is an anti-equivalence; the proof restricts the anti-equivalence of ST02 Corollary 3.3 to the essential image.
The canonical topology of a coadmissible distribution module is nuclear Fréchet, which is needed to apply compact-type duality.

nodes.title: The abelian category of admissible representations
nodes.statement: (i) Rep^a_E(G) is abelian; kernels and images of morphisms are the algebraic kernels and images with the subspace topology. (ii) Every morphism is strict with closed image. (iii) A closed G-stable subspace of an admissible representation is admissible, and so is the quotient by it. (iv) Dually, for a coadmissible M and a submodule N, N is coadmissible ⇔ M/N is ⇔ N is closed; for compact open H, a finitely generated D(H,E)-submodule of a coadmissible D(H,E)-module is coadmissible, finitely generated left ideals of D(H,E) are closed, and finitely presented D(H,E)-modules are coadmissible. (v) A topologically irreducible admissible V has simple dual; an admissible V has finite length if V′ is of finite length as a module, and Jordan–Hölder holds in Rep^a_E(G).
hypotheses: The finite-generation and finite-presentation assertions are over the compact-open algebra D(H,E); finite presentation over noncompact D(G,E) alone does not imply coadmissibility.
proofSteps: Transport the abelian structure of 𝒞_G (ND.2/coadmissible-theorems, LR.1/coadmissible-module) through the anti-equivalence LR.1/admissible-anti-equivalence.

Strictness: the dual of a coadmissible map is a continuous map between compact-type spaces whose dual is strict, so it is strict by the duality of strict morphisms (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0/strict-morphisms-quasi-abelian).
(iii) and (iv) are ST03 Lemma 3.6 transported; (v) follows from (i) and the artinian/noetherian properties of finite-length objects.
acceptance: The locally analytic principal series of GL_2(ℚ_p) of a dominant weight has the locally algebraic representation as a closed subrepresentation and an admissible quotient (LR.4).

sources.match: Admissible representations form an abelian category with algebraic kernels and images, every map is strict with closed image, and the category is closed under passage to closed invariant subspaces.
For a coadmissible module and a submodule, coadmissibility of the submodule, of the quotient, and closedness are equivalent.

Uses these properties of coadmissible modules and admissible representations of GL_2(ℚ_p): finitely generated submodules are coadmissible, finitely generated ideals are closed, maps have closed image.

nodes.title: Admissibility of completed external tensor products
nodes.statement: For admissible locally F-analytic representations V_i of G_i on E-spaces of compact type, the completed external tensor product V_1 ⊠̂_E V_2 is admissible for G_1 × G_2. This asserts external admissibility only; restriction to the diagonal need not preserve admissibility.
hypotheses: E is a finite extension of ℚ_p; use compatible compact-open distribution-algebra Fréchet–Stein presentations for H_1, H_2 and H_1 × H_2.
proofSteps: The compact-type tensor theorem identifies the strong dual with M_1 ⊗̂_E M_2. For compatible radii, D_r(H_1 × H_2,E) is D_r(H_1,E) ⊗̂_E D_r(H_2,E) by the product chart and power-series norm.

The module at radius r is M_{1,r} ⊗̂_E M_{2,r}, finitely generated over the product Banach algebra by pairs of generators. Finite presentations, strict completed tensor products over E, and flat transition base changes identify the radius-transition maps. Taking inverse limits recovers M_1 ⊗̂ M_2 by nuclearity. This is a coadmissible system; apply the anti-equivalence.
acceptance: For V_i=C^an(H_i,E), the result is C^an(H_1 × H_2,E), whose dual is the regular distribution module.
A product of two infinite-dimensional admissible representations is covered, whereas no inference of admissibility after diagonal restriction is allowed.

sources.match: The Levi representation is the completed external tensor product of admissible block representations.
The Orlik–Strauch representation for the product group is expressed as an admissible completed external tensor product.

Compact-type tensor duality and the coherent distribution-module criterion give the proof route above; the admissibility assertion is derived from these inputs, not quoted as an assertion of Proposition 1.1.32.

nodes.title: Locally algebraic representations
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(L) with 𝐆 split reductive over L and E splitting L, and let W be a finite-dimensional algebraic representation of (Res_{L/ℚ_p}𝐆) ×_{ℚ_p} E over E (equivalently of the E-group ∏_{σ∈Σ_L} 𝐆 ×_{L,σ} E), restricted to G. For a smooth admissible representation π of G over E, π ⊗_E W with the diagonal action and the finest locally convex topology is an admissible locally ℚ_p-analytic representation, called locally algebraic. The locally W-algebraic vectors of a locally analytic V are the images of Hom_g(W, V) ⊗ W → V; V is locally algebraic if it is generated by them. If π is irreducible and W is irreducible then π ⊗ W is topologically irreducible (even simple as an E[G]-module).
hypotheses: E large enough that the algebraic representations of (Res_{L/ℚ_p}𝐆) ×_{ℚ_p} E are absolutely irreducible over E.
π smooth admissible; without admissibility π ⊗ W is still locally analytic but not admissible.
proofSteps: π with its finest locally convex topology is an admissible locally analytic representation with trivial derived action (ST03 Theorem 6.6; EM17 Proposition 6.3.2), and the tensor product of an admissible representation with a finite-dimensional locally analytic one is admissible (EM17 Proposition 6.1.5); conversely every admissible locally W-algebraic representation is U ⊗_{End(W)} W with U admissible smooth (EM17 Proposition 6.3.10).
Irreducibility (ST01 Prop. 3.4): every nonzero vector can be moved by elements of a small unipotent subgroup into E_λ ⊗ π^U (highest weight line), and E_λ ⊗ v generates E ⊗ π.

nodes.title: Ext groups of admissible locally analytic representations
nodes.statement: For admissible locally analytic representations V_1, V_2 of G over E put Ext^i_G(V_1, V_2) := Ext^i_{D(G,E)}(V_2′, V_1′), Ext computed in the abelian category Mod(D(G, E)) of all (abstract) left D(G, E)-modules. Variants: for a character χ of the centre Z(G) through which Z(G) acts on V_1 and V_2, Ext^i_{G,χ} is computed over D(G, E) ⊗_{D(Z(G),E)} χ^{-1}; for locally algebraic V_1, V_2, Ext^1_lalg(V_1, V_2) ⊆ Ext^1_G(V_1, V_2) is the subspace of classes whose extension (LR.1/ext1-extensions) is locally algebraic. Ext^i_G is E-linear, contravariant in V_1 and covariant in V_2.
hypotheses: Arguments are reversed: the dual is contravariant.
Ext is taken among all D(G, E)-modules, not among coadmissible ones; LR.1/ext1-extensions shows that Ext^1 nevertheless classifies extensions of admissible representations.
The fixed-character algebra uses χ^{-1} because the chosen left strong dual is contragredient: Z acts on V′ by χ^{-1} when it acts on V by χ.
proofSteps: Mod(D(G, E)) is a Grothendieck abelian category with enough projectives (free modules), so Ext^i is defined (mathlib CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext over ModuleCat D(G, E)).

A strict short exact sequence of admissible representations dualises to a short exact sequence of coadmissible modules (LR.1/admissible-abelian-category), giving the long exact sequences in each variable.
acceptance: Ext^0_G(V_1, V_2) = Hom_G(V_1, V_2) by LR.1/admissible-anti-equivalence.

nodes.title: Ext¹ classifies extensions of admissible representations
nodes.statement: For admissible locally ℚ_p-analytic representations V_1, V_2 of G over E (on spaces of compact type), Ext^1_G(V_1, V_2) is canonically isomorphic to the group of Yoneda classes of extensions 0 → V_2 → V → V_1 → 0 in the category of admissible locally ℚ_p-analytic representations of G (strict exact sequences). The same holds for locally σ-analytic representations with D_σ(G, E) in place of D(G, E).
proofSteps: An extension of admissible representations dualises to an extension of coadmissible modules, hence a class in Ext^1_{D(G,E)}.

Conversely restrict an abstract extension of the duals to D(H,E) for compact open H. Apply the flat Banach-step base changes and compare it with the inverse limit of the resulting extensions. Exactness of the coadmissible inverse-limit rows and a diagram chase recover the original middle module with its canonical topology, as in BR19 Lemma 2.1.1, pp. 10–11. Finite generation at each step alone would not justify this recovery. Dualise the resulting coadmissible extension using LR.1/admissible-anti-equivalence and strictness.
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p, the nonsplit extension of E by E with a ↦ (1 a; 0 1) corresponds to the generator of Ext^1(E, E) = E.

nodes.title: Self-extensions as dual-number modules and tautological extensions
nodes.statement: (i) For Ṽ ∈ Ext^1_G(V, V), the endomorphism ε : Ṽ ↠ V → V ↪ Ṽ (projection followed by inclusion) satisfies ε² = 0 and makes Ṽ a G-equivariant module over E[ε]/(ε²), free with ker ε = im ε = V. (ii) If Ext^1_G(V_1, V_2) is finite-dimensional and U ⊆ Ext^1_G(V_1, V_2) is a subspace, the tautological extension of V_1 ⊗_E U by V_2 is the extension whose class in Ext^1_G(V_1 ⊗_E U, V_2) = Hom_E(U, Ext^1_G(V_1, V_2)) is the inclusion U ↪ Ext^1_G(V_1, V_2); for U = Ext^1_G(V_1, V_2) it is the universal extension of V_1 ⊗_E Ext^1_G(V_1, V_2) by V_2. (iii) For a locally analytic character χ of an abelian group T and ψ ∈ Hom(T, E), the E[ε]/(ε²)-valued character χ(1 + ψε) is a self-extension of χ, and this gives Hom(T, E) ≅ Ext^1_T(χ, χ) (LR.4/torus-ext).
proofSteps: ε² = 0 because the composite V ↪ Ṽ ↠ V is zero; ker ε = V (sub) = im ε by exactness, so Ṽ ≅ V ⊗_E E[ε] as E[ε]-modules after choosing a linear splitting.
Ext^1_G(V_1 ⊗ U, V_2) = Hom_E(U, Ext^1_G(V_1, V_2)) for finite-dimensional U by additivity; the tautological extension is the Yoneda representative of the inclusion (LR.1/ext1-extensions).
acceptance: For U′ ⊆ U, pull back the extension along V_1 ⊗ U′ → V_1 ⊗ U. For f : V_2 → W, its pushout represents the map U → Ext¹_G(V_1,W) obtained by applying f_* to the inclusion. If that map has a kernel, it is not automatically the tautological extension indexed by its image; passing to that image changes the quotient and requires a further pullback comparison.

nodes.title: Ext groups between locally algebraic representations
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(L) with 𝐆 split reductive, F_λ, F_μ irreducible finite-dimensional algebraic representations of (Res_{L/ℚ_p}𝐆) ×_{ℚ_p} E of highest weights λ, μ, and W_1, W_2 smooth admissible representations of G. (1) If λ ≠ μ then Ext^n_G(F_λ ⊗ W_1, F_μ ⊗ W_2) = 0 for all n. (2) If W_1, W_2 have trivial central character and i_0 is the least i with Ext^i_{∞,1}(W_1, W_2) ≠ 0 (smooth Ext with trivial central character), then Ext^n_{G,λ}(F_λ ⊗ W_1, F_λ ⊗ W_2) ≅ Ext^{i_0}_{∞,1}(W_1, W_2) for n = i_0 and vanishes for n ≠ i_0, n ≤ i_0 + 2. In particular, for central character fixed, Ext^1_{lalg,Z}(π_alg, π_alg) → Ext^1_{G,Z}(π_alg, π_alg) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Central characters fixed in (2); E large enough to split the algebraic representations.
proofSteps: The centre Z(g) of U(g ⊗ E) acts on F_λ ⊗ W through the infinitesimal character of λ (LieHighestWeight Layer 7); distinct dominant λ ≠ μ have distinct infinitesimal characters, and an element of Z(g) acting by different scalars kills the Ext groups (the standard central-character argument, as for SR.0:derived-extension/central-ext-vanishing).

For λ = μ, Schraen computes Ext_{G,λ} through the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for g ⊂ D(G) and Lie algebra cohomology of F_λ, which is concentrated in degrees where it reduces to smooth Ext (SCH11 Prop. 4.7 proof).
acceptance: For GL_2(ℚ_p), Ext^1(Sym^k ⊗ 1, Sym^{k'} ⊗ 1) = 0 for k ≠ k'.

nodes.title: Admissible Banach representations of p-adic groups
nodes.statement: Let G be a locally ℚ_p-analytic group and E/ℚ_p finite with ring of integers O_E. A Banach representation of G over E is an E-Banach space B with a G-action by continuous linear maps such that G × B → B is continuous. It is admissible if its restriction to one (equivalently every) compact open subgroup H is admissible in the sense of LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.6/banach-iwasawa-duality, i.e. B′ is finitely generated over E[[H]] = E ⊗_{O_E} O_E[[H]]; it is unitary if it has a G-invariant open bounded lattice. Ban^adm_E(G) is the category of admissible Banach representations with continuous G-maps; it is abelian, every morphism is strict, and B ↦ B′ is an anti-equivalence of the unitary admissible part with finitely generated E[[H]]-modules carrying a compatible G-action (Schneider–Teitelbaum).
hypotheses: Admissibility does not require unitarity; finite-dimensional continuous representations are admissible Banach representations.
Independence of H: for H′ ⊆ H open, E[[H]] is finite free over E[[H′]].
proofSteps: For compact open H′ ⊆ H, E[[H]] is a finite free E[[H′]]-module, so finite generation of B′ over E[[H]] and over E[[H′]] are equivalent; this gives independence of H.
Abelianness and strictness are ND.6/banach-iwasawa-duality for compact open H together with the open mapping theorem (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0/banach-open-mapping-lifts).
acceptance: For compact G, Ban^adm_E(G) is the category of ND.6/banach-iwasawa-duality.

nodes.title: Analytic and locally analytic vectors of a Banach representation
nodes.statement: Let B be a Banach representation of G over E, G_0 ⊆ G a compact open subgroup carrying an integral saturated p-valuation with an ordered basis (LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.0), and G_n = G_0^{p^n}. C^an(G_n, B) is the Banach space of B-valued functions given in the coordinates of the ordered basis by power series Σ b_k x^k with p^{n|k|} b_k → 0, normed by sup ‖p^{n|k|} b_k‖, and C^an(G_n, B) ≅ C^an(G_n, ℚ_p) ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} B. The G_n-analytic vectors B^{G_n-an} are the vectors whose orbit map lies in C^an(G_n, B); equivalently B^{G_n-an} = (C^an(G_n, ℚ_p) ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} B)^{G_n} for the diagonal action, embedded in B by evaluation at 1, with the norm ‖·‖_{G_n}. B^{la} := colim_n B^{G_n-an} with the inductive-limit topology is the space of locally analytic vectors; it is G-stable, independent of G_0, carries a continuous injection B^la → B, and is a locally analytic representation of G on an LB-space. The derived g-action on B^{G_n-an} is bounded: ‖D(x)‖_{G_n} ≤ C_{D,n}‖x‖_{G_n}.
hypotheses: Fix the integral saturated p-valued subgroup G_0. The spaces and norms are independent of its ordered basis (Pan §2.1.1, p. 11); changing G_0 changes the presentation but not B^la. The stated bounded Lie action on a radius space uses n ≥ 1 (Lemma 2.1.8).
proofSteps: Independence of the ordered basis: coordinates of the first and second kind differ by power series with ℤ_p-coefficients (Pan I §2.1.1, via SCHN11 §34).
B^{G_n-an} ⊆ B^{G_{n+1}-an} with ‖·‖_{G_{n+1}} ≤ ‖·‖_{G_n} (Pan I Lemma 2.1.5), so the colimit is an LB-space; G-stability follows by conjugating G_0.
Orbit maps of vectors of B^{G_n-an} are analytic on cosets of G_n, so B^la is locally analytic (LR.0/locally-analytic-representation); the Lie bound is Pan I Lemma 2.1.8.
acceptance: For B finite-dimensional, B^la = B; for B = C(ℤ_p, E) with translation, B^la = C^la(ℤ_p, E) (Amice, LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0).

nodes.title: Locally analytic vectors of admissible Banach representations
nodes.statement: Let B be an admissible Banach representation of G over E. Then: (i) B^la is dense in B; (ii) B^la is a strongly admissible locally analytic representation of G; (iii) as a D(H,E)-module, (B^la)′ ≅ D(H,E) ⊗_{E[[H]]} B′ for a compact open H, with the compatible G-action inherited from B; (iv) the functor Ban^adm_E(G) → Rep^a_E(G), B ↦ B^la, is exact.
proofSteps: Reduce to G compact. The dual of B^la is computed Banach level by level; D(G, E) is (faithfully) flat over E[[G]] (ND.2/faithful-flatness), which gives (iii) and the exactness (iv).

(iii) shows (B^la)′ is finitely generated over D(G, E), hence (ii); faithful flatness and the injectivity E[[G]] ⊂ D(G, E) (ND.1/iwasawa-to-distributions) give injectivity of B′ → (B^la)′, i.e. density (i).
acceptance: For B = C(G_0, E) (G_0 compact), B^la = C^la(G_0, E) with dual D(G_0, E) = D(G_0, E) ⊗_{E[[G_0]]} E[[G_0]].

sources.match: For compact G, Theorem 7.1 gives density, strong admissibility, the dual D(G,E) ⊗_{E[[G]]} B′, and exactness. For general G these conclusions are checked after restriction to compact open H; the displayed base change then uses D(H,E).

nodes.title: Very strongly admissible representations
nodes.statement: An admissible locally analytic representation V of G over E is very strongly admissible if there is a continuous G-equivariant E-linear injection V → B into an admissible Banach representation B of G. Very strongly admissible representations are strongly admissible; for compact G the converse holds; closed subrepresentations of very strongly admissible representations are very strongly admissible; and for every admissible Banach representation Π, Π^la (= Π^an) is very strongly admissible.
hypotheses: The Banach target need not be unitary.
proofSteps: Strong admissibility: the injection V → B factors through B^la, which is strongly admissible (LR.2/admissible-banach-analytic-vectors), and V is a closed subrepresentation of it (morphisms of admissible representations have closed image, LR.1/admissible-abelian-category).
Π^an ⊂ Π is the required injection for Π admissible Banach.

nodes.title: Derived functors of locally analytic vectors
nodes.statement: For a Banach representation B of G (with G_0, G_n as in LR.2/analytic-vectors) put R^iLA(B) := colim_n H^i_cont(G_n, B ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} C^an(G_n, ℚ_p)), continuous group cohomology for the diagonal action. R^0LA(B) = B^la. B is LA-acyclic if R^iLA(B) = 0 for all i ≥ 1, and strongly LA-acyclic if for every i ≥ 1 the direct system (H^i_cont(G_n, B ⊗̂ C^an(G_n, ℚ_p)))_n is essentially zero (for each n the transition map to some m ≥ n is zero). These do not depend on G_0.
hypotheses: Continuous cohomology of the profinite group G_n with coefficients in a Banach representation (mathlib continuousCohomology over TopModuleCat).
proofSteps: H^0_cont(G_n, B ⊗̂ C^an(G_n)) = (C^an(G_n, B))^{G_n} = B^{G_n-an}, so R^0LA(B) = B^la.
Independence of G_0: G_n for two choices are cofinal in each other, and the systems are isomorphic as ind-objects.
acceptance: For finite-dimensional continuous B, Pan Theorem 2.2.3, p. 14, implies higher R^iLA(B)=0. Analytic functions are not the full continuous coinduced module, so a continuous Shapiro argument alone would not prove this.

nodes.title: Long exact sequence of derived locally analytic vectors
nodes.statement: (1) A short exact sequence 0 → M_0 → M_1 → M_2 → 0 of Banach representations of G with continuous (hence strict) G-maps gives a long exact sequence 0 → M_0^la → M_1^la → M_2^la → R^1LA(M_0) → R^1LA(M_1) → R^1LA(M_2) → ⋯. (2) For a bounded complex M^• of Banach representations with strict G-maps, if each M^q and each H^q(M^•) is LA-acyclic then H^q(M^•)^la = H^q((M^•)^la). (3) If 0 → B → M^0 → M^1 → ⋯ is exact with strict maps and each M^q is LA-acyclic, then R^iLA(B) = H^i((M^•)^la); if moreover each M^q is strongly LA-acyclic and the systems (H^i((M^•)^{G_n-an}))_n are essentially zero for i ≥ 1, then B is strongly LA-acyclic.
proofSteps: Strictness bounds the p-torsion in the cohomology of the unit balls, so M^• ⊗̂ C^an(G_n, ℚ_p) stays exact; taking continuous G_n-cohomology and the colimit over n gives (1).
(2) and (3) follow from (1) by induction on the length, showing kernels and images are LA-acyclic.
acceptance: Applied to 0 → B → C(G_0, E)^{⊕d} → C → 0 for admissible B it is the first step of the proof of LR.2/admissible-la-acyclic.

sources.match: Gives the long exact sequence for strict short exact sequences of Banach representations, the comparison of cohomology of complexes with locally analytic vectors under LA-acyclicity, and the acyclic-resolution computation of R^iLA.

nodes.title: Admissible Banach representations are strongly LA-acyclic
nodes.statement: Every admissible Banach representation B of G is strongly LA-acyclic, and so is B ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} M for every ℚ_p-Banach space M with trivial G-action. If G is compact, the inclusion B^la → B also induces H^i_cont(G, B^la) ≅ H^i_cont(G, B) for all i (continuous cohomology of B equals that of its locally analytic vectors).
hypotheses: The cohomology comparison here is restricted to compact G, as in RJRC22 Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 1.6. The strong LA-acyclicity statement is local on compact opens and applies to general G.
proofSteps: Embed B G_0-equivariantly into C(G_0, ℚ_p)^{⊕d} with admissible quotient C (admissibility).

C(G_0, ℚ_p) ≅ C(G_n, ℚ_p)^{⊕d_n} as G_n-representations, so its H^1 with coefficients in ⊗̂ C^an(G_n) vanishes by Shapiro's lemma; the long exact sequence (LR.2/la-long-exact-sequence) and Colmez–Dospinescu's comparison of G_n-analytic vectors with the C^{(m)} filtration show the transition maps H^1 → H^1 vanish; induct on i.
For B ⊗̂ M, H^•_cont(G_n, B ⊗̂ M) = H^•_cont(G_n, B) ⊗̂ M because the cochain complex of B is strict (finite generation of H^•_cont(G_n, B°) over ℤ_p).

The compact-group cohomology comparison uses the derived locally analytic vector/cohomology theorem of RJRC22 Theorem 1.5 and Corollary 1.6, p. 5, followed by the vanishing of higher analytic vectors. This is a separate non-routine comparison input; see the recorded proof contract. No noncompact comparison is inferred merely by restriction.
acceptance: For B = C(G_0, E), R^iLA(B) = 0 for i ≥ 1 and B^la = C^la(G_0, E).

sources.locator: §2.2, Theorem 2.2.3 and Corollary 2.2.4 with proofs, pp. 13–14
sources.match: Admissible Banach representations are strongly LA-acyclic, via an embedding into C(G_0, ℚ_p)^{⊕d}, Shapiro's lemma and Colmez–Dospinescu's control of analytic vectors; the statement persists after completed tensor product with a trivial Banach space.
If V has no higher locally analytic vectors (as for admissible representations) then H^i_cont(G, V) = H^i_cont(G, V^la).

nodes.title: Solid representations of an analytic group
nodes.statement: Let 𝔾 be a Stein analytic group over Spa(E, O_E) (the analytification of an affine algebraic group over E, or a quasi-compact affinoid open subgroup of one; quasi-Stein and Stein as in AdicSpacesPartII R3), with Fréchet Hopf algebra of functions O_𝔾 ∈ Mod(E). A solid representation of 𝔾 is a solid E-vector space V with a coaction c : V → V ⊗_E O_𝔾 satisfying coassociativity (c ⊗ id) ∘ c = (id ⊗ μ) ∘ c and counitality (id ⊗ e) ∘ c = id; Mod_𝔾(E) denotes their category, B_𝔾(E) and LB_𝔾(E) the full subcategories of representations on Banach and LB spaces. The distribution algebra is D(𝔾) := Hom_E(O_𝔾, E) = O_𝔾^∨, with product dual to the comultiplication, and every V ∈ Mod_𝔾(E) is a D(𝔾)-module through V ⊗ D(𝔾) → V ⊗ O_𝔾 ⊗ D(𝔾) → V. Four predicates on a group action are kept distinct: an analytic 𝔾-action (a coaction as above), a continuous action of the locally profinite group 𝔾(E) (LR.3/solid-group-representation), analyticity at a Banach stage (LR.3/solid-analytic-vectors), and an algebraic coaction (ReductiveGroups Layer 1).
hypotheses: Solid conventions (BCGP25 §2.2, recalled from Rodrigues Jacinto–Rodríguez Camargo): a fixed strongly inaccessible cardinal κ bounds all profinite sets; E/ℚ_p finite; Mod(E) is the category of solid E-vector spaces, modules over the analytic ring E_■ = (E, O_E)_■ of SolidAnalyticRings SA.4; tensor products and internal Homs are solid. This is not the predicate IsSolid on arbitrary condensed modules over a general ring.
proofSteps: The coaction axioms are those of an algebraic comodule (ReductiveGroups Layer 1) with O_𝔾 a Fréchet Hopf algebra in Mod(E).
The D(𝔾)-module structure is the composite of the coaction with evaluation O_𝔾 ⊗ D(𝔾) → E, associative because the product of D(𝔾) is dual to μ.
acceptance: Analytifying an algebraic coaction gives a solid analytic representation. The converse for arbitrary finite-dimensional analytic representations is not asserted; for a small additive analytic disc, nonpolynomial exponential characters provide analytic examples.

uses.how: Banach representations of a quasi-compact 𝔾 are the same as Banach D(𝔾)-modules
V^{M_r-an} = H⁰(M_r, O_{𝔾_r} ⊗ V), the analytic vectors for the polydisc subgroups 𝔾_r

nodes.title: Banach representations of a quasi-compact analytic group
nodes.statement: For a quasi-compact analytic group 𝔾 and a Banach space V, Hom_E(D(𝔾), V) = O_𝔾 ⊗_E V; consequently every D(𝔾)-module structure on V comes from a unique coaction, and the functor of LR.3/solid-analytic-group-representation restricts to an equivalence B_𝔾(E) ≃ B(D(𝔾)) between Banach representations of 𝔾 and D(𝔾)-modules whose underlying space is Banach.
hypotheses: Solid conventions (BCGP25 §2.2, recalled from Rodrigues Jacinto–Rodríguez Camargo): a fixed strongly inaccessible cardinal κ bounds all profinite sets; E/ℚ_p finite; Mod(E) is the category of solid E-vector spaces, modules over the analytic ring E_■ = (E, O_E)_■ of SolidAnalyticRings SA.4; tensor products and internal Homs are solid. This is not the predicate IsSolid on arbitrary condensed modules over a general ring.
Quasi-compactness of 𝔾 makes O_𝔾 a Banach space and D(𝔾) a Smith space; this is the input taken from the solid functional analysis recorded in the gap 'Solid functional analysis'.
proofSteps: D(𝔾) = O_𝔾^∨ is a Smith space, so Hom_E(D(𝔾), V) = O_𝔾 ⊗_E V for Banach V (RJRC22 Corollary 3.17).
A module map D(𝔾) ⊗ V → V corresponds to V → Hom(D(𝔾), V) = O_𝔾 ⊗ V, and the module axioms correspond to the comodule axioms.
acceptance: For 𝔾 = 1 both sides are the category of Banach spaces.

sources.match: For quasi-compact G and Banach V, Hom(D(G), V) = O_G ⊗ V (citing RJRC22 Corollary 3.17), so D(G)-module structures on V give G-actions and B_G(E) ≃ B(D(G)).
For V Banach and W Smith, the internal Hom and tensor product are related so that Hom(W, V) = W^∨ ⊗ V; applied with W = D(𝔾) a Smith space.

nodes.title: Solid representations of a locally profinite group
nodes.statement: Let M be a locally profinite group, viewed as a condensed group, E[M] its condensed group ring and E_■[M] its solidification: for compact M, E_■[M] = (lim_N O_E[M/N])[1/p] over open normal N; in general E_■[M] = E[M] ⊗_{E[M_0]} E_■[M_0] for any compact open M_0 ⊆ M. A representation of M on a solid E-vector space is a solid E_■[M]-module; equivalently a solid E-vector space V with an action map M × V → V of condensed sets satisfying the group action axioms. Mod_M(E) denotes this category.
hypotheses: Solid conventions (BCGP25 §2.2, recalled from Rodrigues Jacinto–Rodríguez Camargo): a fixed strongly inaccessible cardinal κ bounds all profinite sets; E/ℚ_p finite; Mod(E) is the category of solid E-vector spaces, modules over the analytic ring E_■ = (E, O_E)_■ of SolidAnalyticRings SA.4; tensor products and internal Homs are solid. This is not the predicate IsSolid on arbitrary condensed modules over a general ring.
proofSteps: For compact M, E_■[M] is the rational Iwasawa algebra with its weak (compact) topology as a solid algebra; the induction formula defines E_■[M] for general M independently of M_0 because E_■[M_0] is free over E_■[M_1] for M_1 ⊆ M_0 open (finite index).
Action maps M × V → V of condensed sets correspond to E[M]-module structures, and solidity of V makes them extend uniquely to E_■[M].
acceptance: A continuous representation of M on a complete locally convex E-vector space gives, through the condensed-set functor, an object of Mod_M(E).

nodes.title: Smooth and λ-smooth solid representations
nodes.statement: For V ∈ Mod_M(E) put V^sm := colim_N V^N over compact open subgroups N ⊆ M (invariants in Mod(E)); V is smooth if V^sm → V is an isomorphism; Mod^sm_M(E) is the full subcategory of smooth representations. For a continuous character λ : M → E^× and E(−λ) the corresponding one-dimensional representation of λ^{-1}, V is λ-smooth if V ⊗_E E(−λ) is smooth; Mod^{λ-sm}_M(E) is the category of λ-smooth representations, and if λ ⊗ λ′^{-1} is smooth then Mod^{λ-sm}_M(E) and Mod^{λ′-sm}_M(E) are canonically equivalent (equal as subcategories).
hypotheses: Solid conventions (BCGP25 §2.2, recalled from Rodrigues Jacinto–Rodríguez Camargo): a fixed strongly inaccessible cardinal κ bounds all profinite sets; E/ℚ_p finite; Mod(E) is the category of solid E-vector spaces, modules over the analytic ring E_■ = (E, O_E)_■ of SolidAnalyticRings SA.4; tensor products and internal Homs are solid. This is not the predicate IsSolid on arbitrary condensed modules over a general ring.
proofSteps: V^N is a closed subobject of V in Mod(E); filtered colimits exist, so V^sm is defined, with a natural map to V.
If λ/λ′ is smooth then V ⊗ E(−λ) and V ⊗ E(−λ′) differ by tensoring with a smooth character, which preserves smoothness.
acceptance: A countable-dimensional classical smooth representation with its finest locally convex E-topology gives a solid smooth object, via its presentation as a filtered union of finite-dimensional E-spaces. E itself always retains its p-adic topology.

nodes.title: Smooth solid representations are smooth representations of the discrete group
nodes.statement: Let M_disc be M with the discrete topology and Mod^sm_{M_disc}(E) the category of E[M_disc]-modules V in Mod(E) with V = colim_N V^{N_disc}. Restriction along M_disc → M induces an equivalence Mod^sm_M(E) ≃ Mod^sm_{M_disc}(E).
hypotheses: Solid conventions (BCGP25 §2.2, recalled from Rodrigues Jacinto–Rodríguez Camargo): a fixed strongly inaccessible cardinal κ bounds all profinite sets; E/ℚ_p finite; Mod(E) is the category of solid E-vector spaces, modules over the analytic ring E_■ = (E, O_E)_■ of SolidAnalyticRings SA.4; tensor products and internal Homs are solid. This is not the predicate IsSolid on arbitrary condensed modules over a general ring.
The subscript disc changes the topology of the group M only. The coefficient ring remains the solid analytic ring E_■ on both sides.
proofSteps: The functor Mod_M(E) → Mod_{M_disc}(E) preserves smoothness.

Inverse: for smooth V over M_disc and a cofinal system of open normal M_n ⊆ M_0, V^{M_n} is an E[M_0/M_n]-module and (M_0)_disc/(M_n)_disc = M_0/M_n, so the action extends uniquely to M_0; pass to the colimit and use E[M] = E[M_disc] ⊗_{E[(M_0)_disc]} E[M_0].
acceptance: For M = ℤ_p the smooth objects on both sides are colimits of representations of the finite groups ℤ/p^n.

sources.match: The categories of smooth solid M-representations and of smooth M_disc-representations are equivalent: on N-invariants for open normal N ⊆ M_0 the M_0/N-action is that of a finite group, so the discrete action extends uniquely.

nodes.title: Smooth solid representations form a Grothendieck category
nodes.statement: With the fixed cardinal bound κ on profinite sets, Mod^sm_M(E) is a Grothendieck abelian category; ⊕_{S,N} E_■[M] ⊗_{E_■[N]} E_■[S] over κ-small profinite (totally disconnected) S and compact open N ⊆ M (with N acting trivially on E_■[S]) is a generator, since Hom(E_■[M] ⊗_{E_■[N]} E_■[S], V) = V^N(S). In particular Mod^sm_M(E) has enough injectives.
hypotheses: Solid conventions (BCGP25 §2.2, recalled from Rodrigues Jacinto–Rodríguez Camargo): a fixed strongly inaccessible cardinal κ bounds all profinite sets; E/ℚ_p finite; Mod(E) is the category of solid E-vector spaces, modules over the analytic ring E_■ = (E, O_E)_■ of SolidAnalyticRings SA.4; tensor products and internal Homs are solid. This is not the predicate IsSolid on arbitrary condensed modules over a general ring.
proofSteps: Colimits exist and filtered colimits are exact (AB5) because both hold in Mod(E) and invariants under compact open N commute with filtered colimits of smooth objects.
The displayed generator corepresents V ↦ V^N(S); every V is a quotient of a sum of these. A Grothendieck abelian category has enough injectives.
acceptance: For classical countable-dimensional smooth representations given the finest locally convex E-topology, the terms with S a point are the usual compact inductions c-Ind_N^M E of the smooth supplier, with p-adic E coefficients. The additional profinite S detect all solid sections.

sources.match: The category of smooth solid representations is Grothendieck abelian with generator built from compact inductions of free solid modules on profinite sets, hence has enough injectives (Stacks Tag 079H).
The argument uses the set-theoretic restriction to κ-small profinite sets.

nodes.title: Locally analytic vectors of solid representations
nodes.statement: Assume M = 𝔾(ℚ_p) for an analytic group 𝔾 over Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) with a fundamental system of quasi-compact open subgroups 𝔾_r (r ≥ 0), each a polydisc, and put M_r := 𝔾_r(ℚ_p), a fundamental system of compact open subgroups. Put O_{𝔾_r,E} := O_{𝔾_r} ⊗_{ℚ_p} E. For V ∈ Mod_M(E), O_{𝔾_r,E} ⊗_E V carries three commuting actions of M_r: ∗_l (left translation on 𝔾_r), ∗_r (right translation) and ∗_V (from V; this one extends to M, which acts on {M_r} by conjugation). Define V^{M_r-an} := H^0(M_r, O_{𝔾_r,E} ⊗_E V) for the diagonal action ∗_l ⊗ ∗_V; it keeps the residual action ∗_r of M_r, which commutes with ∗_l ⊗ ∗_V, and evaluation at e gives an M_r-equivariant injection V^{M_r-an} → V. Then V^la := colim_r V^{M_r-an} ∈ Mod_M(E), with natural injections V^sm → V^la → V. The derived functor is V^{Rla} := hocolim_r RHom_{E_■[M_r]}(E, V ⊗^L_E O_{𝔾_r,E}) (Rodrigues Jacinto–Rodríguez Camargo), with H^0(V^{Rla}) = V^la; for V a Banach representation, V^la is the classical space of locally analytic vectors (LR.2/analytic-vectors) and H^i(V^{Rla}) = R^iLA(V) (LR.2/derived-analytic-vectors).
hypotheses: Solid conventions (BCGP25 §2.2, recalled from Rodrigues Jacinto–Rodríguez Camargo): a fixed strongly inaccessible cardinal κ bounds all profinite sets; E/ℚ_p finite; Mod(E) is the category of solid E-vector spaces, modules over the analytic ring E_■ = (E, O_E)_■ of SolidAnalyticRings SA.4; tensor products and internal Homs are solid. This is not the predicate IsSolid on arbitrary condensed modules over a general ring.
The polydisc subgroups 𝔾_r come from an ordered-basis chart of a uniform open subgroup (RJRC22 Remark 1.4), consistent with the G_n of LR.2/analytic-vectors.

Every occurrence of O_{𝔾_r} with E-coefficients means O_{𝔾_r,E}=O_{𝔾_r} ⊗_{ℚ_p} E, including in the derived formula. The derived Banach comparison is the proof contract recorded under derived analytic vectors.
proofSteps: O_{𝔾_r,E} ⊗_E V is a solid M_r-representation for each of the three actions; invariants for ∗_l ⊗ ∗_V are a left exact functor.

Evaluation at e intertwines the residual right-translation action ∗_r on the invariant functions with the given action on V. There is no extra tensor factor ∗_V in this residual action. An invariant function is its orbit function and is determined by its value at e.

For Banach V, O_{𝔾_r,E} ⊗_E V is the completed projective tensor product (RJRC22 §1.2.2), so the invariants are V^{G_r-an} of LR.2/analytic-vectors; the derived version is computed by continuous cohomology, giving R^iLA.
acceptance: For V = O_{𝔾_0} with the right regular action, V^{M_0-an} = V.

nodes.title: Integrable LB representations of a Lie algebra
nodes.statement: Let g be the E-Lie algebra of the analytic group germ 𝔾_e. An LB representation here is a continuous module V over the Arens–Michael completion Û(g), presented by an increasing sequence of Banach subspaces V_r with injective transition maps. It is integrable if these subspaces are g-stable and, after a cofinal reindexing, V_r carries an analytic action of a shrinking analytic subgroup 𝔾_r whose derivative is the given action and whose restriction agrees with the action at later stages. The result is an action of the analytic group germ on V: each stage integrates on a suitable neighbourhood. This does not assert an action of one fixed 𝔾_r on all of V.
hypotheses: Solid conventions (BCGP25 §2.2, recalled from Rodrigues Jacinto–Rodríguez Camargo): a fixed strongly inaccessible cardinal κ bounds all profinite sets; E/ℚ_p finite; Mod(E) is the category of solid E-vector spaces, modules over the analytic ring E_■ = (E, O_E)_■ of SolidAnalyticRings SA.4; tensor products and internal Homs are solid. This is not the predicate IsSolid on arbitrary condensed modules over a general ring.

The completed enveloping algebra Û(g) and its germ-distribution identification are imported from LocallyAnalyticDistributionsPartII ND.3/arens-michael-envelope. Parabolic category O is an application context in BCGP, not data in the definition of integrability.
proofSteps: Uniqueness of the integration: two analytic 𝔾_r-actions with the same derivative agree on 𝔾_r for r large (the exponential is a local isomorphism near 0; LR.0/rational-points-analytic-group).
Banach analytic representations are Banach D(𝔾_r)-modules (LR.3/banach-analytic-comparison), so integrability is a condition on the g-action extending to D(𝔾_r) on V_r.
acceptance: A finite-dimensional algebraic representation of 𝔾 is integrable for the constant filtration.

nodes.title: Locally analytic parabolic induction
nodes.statement: Let G = 𝐆(L) with 𝐆 connected reductive over L, P = M_P N_P a parabolic subgroup (so P\G is compact by the Iwasawa decomposition G = P·K_0, ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4), and U a locally F-analytic representation of P on a space of compact type. The locally analytic induction is (Ind_P^G U)^{F-an} := {f ∈ C^{F-an}(G, U) : f(pg) = p·f(g) for p ∈ P, g ∈ G}, with G acting by right translation (g·f)(h) = f(hg). It is a closed subspace of C^{F-an}(G, U), of compact type, and a locally F-analytic representation of G. If U is inflated from a locally analytic representation of M_P which is admissible (respectively strongly admissible, very strongly admissible), the induction has the corresponding property. Induction is transitive, (Ind_P^G (Ind_Q^P U)^an)^an ≅ (Ind_Q^G U)^an for Q ⊆ P, exact on strict short exact sequences, and contains (Ind_P^G π)^∞ ⊗ W, the locally algebraic induction (Ind_P^G π ⊗ W|_P)^{lalg}, for π smooth admissible of M_P inflated to P and W algebraic of 𝐆. Parabolic inductions are unnormalised ('droites'). For F = ℚ_p and σ ∈ Σ_L the locally σ-analytic induction (Ind_P^G U)^{σ-an} ⊆ (Ind_P^G U)^{ℚ_p-an} consists of the functions whose derived g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E-action factors through g_σ (LR.9/sigma-analytic-representation).
hypotheses: P\G compact (Iwasawa decomposition), so that functions are determined on a compact set and the induction is of compact type.

U is of compact type. An arbitrary infinite-dimensional Banach U does not acquire this property merely by taking analytic functions: constant U-valued functions already give a closed copy of U in the local function space.
proofSteps: Choose local analytic sections of G → P\G over a finite disjoint compact-open cover. The induction is topologically a finite product of compact-base analytic function spaces with compact-type coefficients U, hence of compact type. Closedness in C^an(G,U) alone does not give compact type for noncompact G.

For U inflated from M_P, EMJ2 Proposition 2.1.2 proves preservation of the three admissibility conditions using analytic Banach-stage embeddings and the compact-base description. The general dual uses a completed balanced tensor product; BR16 Lemma 2.2 identifies only a dense algebraic image for arbitrary smooth inducing coefficients.
Transitivity: the map f ↦ (g ↦ f(g)(1)) is an isomorphism, as for smooth induction (SR.2/induction-in-stages).

For f in the smooth induction and w ∈ W, send f ⊗ w to the function g ↦ f(g) ⊗ g·w. Its P-transformation and right G-equivariance give the tensor identity and the locally algebraic injection. The constant function g ↦ f(g) ⊗ w would not satisfy the required transformation law.
acceptance: For G = GL_2(ℚ_p), P = B^- and a locally analytic character χ, (Ind_{B^-}^G χ)^an ≅ C^an(ℙ^1(ℚ_p), E) as topological vector spaces.

nodes.title: Locally analytic principal series
nodes.statement: Let 𝐆 be split reductive over L with split maximal torus 𝐓 ⊆ 𝐁 = 𝐓𝐍 (Borel, unipotent radical 𝐍) and opposite Borel 𝐁^-, G = 𝐆(L), T = 𝐓(L). For a locally ℚ_p-analytic character χ : T → E^×, inflated to B^- = B^-(L), the locally analytic principal series is PS(χ) := (Ind_{B^-}^G χ)^{ℚ_p-an} (LR.4/locally-analytic-induction). Its derivative dχ ∈ Hom(t ⊗_{ℚ_p} E, E) = ∏_σ t_σ^* is its weight. For χ = χ_sm z^λ with χ_sm smooth and λ = (λ_{σ,i})_{σ∈Σ_L, 1≤i≤n} an algebraic weight (for GL_n, z^λ(diag(t_1, …, t_n)) = ∏_{σ,i} σ(t_i)^{λ_{σ,i}}), and λ dominant with respect to 𝐁, PS(χ) contains (Ind_{B^-}^G χ_sm)^∞ ⊗_E L(λ) as its locally algebraic vectors, where L(λ) is the irreducible algebraic representation of (Res_{L/ℚ_p}𝐆) ×_{ℚ_p} E of highest weight λ.
hypotheses: E splits L and contains the values of χ.
Unnormalised induction from the lower Borel B^-, Ding's convention.
proofSteps: PS(χ) is admissible, very strongly admissible when χ is (characters are finite-dimensional, LR.2/very-strongly-admissible), by LR.4/locally-analytic-induction.

The locally algebraic vectors are computed by the inclusion of LR.4/locally-analytic-induction with W = L(λ): for dominant λ the highest-weight line of L(λ) is the unique B^--stable quotient line (n^- lowers weights), on which B^- acts by z^λ; Frobenius reciprocity identifies (Ind χ_sm)^∞ ⊗ L(λ) with the locally algebraic induction.
acceptance: For GL_2(ℚ_p) and χ = z^λ with λ = (k, 0), k ≥ 0, PS(χ)_lalg = (Ind_{B^-}^G 1)^∞ ⊗ Sym^k(E²).

nodes.title: Ext groups between locally analytic characters of a torus
nodes.statement: Let T = 𝐓(L) for a split torus 𝐓 ≅ 𝔾_m^n over L, and χ, χ′ : T → E^× locally ℚ_p-analytic characters. (1) If χ ≠ χ′ then Ext^i_T(χ, χ′) = 0 for all i. (2) Ext^1_T(χ, χ) ≅ Hom(T, E), the E-vector space of locally ℚ_p-analytic additive characters T → E, via ψ ↦ χ(1 + ψε) (LR.1/self-extension-dual-numbers). (3) dim_E Hom(L^×, E) = 1 + d_L, dim_E Hom_sm(L^×, E) = 1 and dim_E Hom_σ(L^×, E) = 2 for σ ∈ Σ_L, where Hom_sm consists of smooth (locally constant) and Hom_σ of locally σ-analytic characters (dψ factoring through Lie(L^×) ⊗_{L,σ} E); hence dim Hom(T, E) = n(1 + d_L) and dim Hom_sm(T, E) = n. (4) Hom_{g′}(GL_n) := {ψ ∈ Hom(T(L), E) : ψ − ψ_0 ∘ det ∈ Hom_sm(T(L), E) for some ψ_0 ∈ Hom(L^×, E)} has dimension n + d_L.
hypotheses: T abelian, so D(T, E) is commutative.
proofSteps: (1): D(T, E) is commutative; if χ ≠ χ′ there is t ∈ T with χ(t) ≠ χ′(t) (or x ∈ t with dχ(x) ≠ dχ′(x)); the central element δ_t − χ(t) acts by 0 on χ and invertibly on χ′, hence by both 0 and an isomorphism on the Ext groups.
(2): a self-extension of the character χ is a two-dimensional representation, upper triangular with a locally analytic additive character in the corner; normalising by χ gives ψ.
(3): L^× ≅ ϖ^ℤ × μ × (1 + ϖ^m O_L) with 1 + ϖ^m O_L ≅ O_L ≅ ℤ_p^{d_L} for m large; additive characters are the valuation (smooth) and the E-linear combinations of σ ∘ log (σ ∈ Σ_L).
(4): Hom_{g′} is the sum of Hom_sm(T, E) (dimension n) and det^*Hom(L^×, E) (dimension 1 + d_L), meeting in det^*Hom_sm(L^×, E) (dimension 1).
acceptance: For n = 1 and L = ℚ_p, Ext^1_{ℚ_p^×}(1, 1) is two-dimensional, spanned by the valuation and log_p.

nodes.title: Homology of locally analytic representations under a unipotent radical
nodes.statement: For a locally analytic N-representation V, define H_q(N,V) as the homology, with its subquotient topology, of Kohlhaase’s topological bar complex B_•(N,V) ⊗̃_{D(N,E),ι} E. The bar construction is the standard simplicial resolution of the free/forgetful cotriple F(X)=D(N,E) ⊗̂_{E,ι} X; its differential is the alternating sum of faces. These homology spaces need not be Hausdorff. If V is of compact type and is a P=M_PN_P-representation, then Hausdorff H_q(N_P,V) are compact-type locally analytic M_P-representations. For V=W ⊗ π locally algebraic, H_q(N_P,V) ≅ H_q(n_P,W) ⊗_E J_{N_P}(π), where J is the unnormalised smooth Jacquet module. For finite-dimensional W, compute the Lie homology by the M_P-equivariant duality H_q(n_P,W) ≅ H^q(n_P,W∨)∨ and Kostant’s cohomology theorem, keeping the dual and the exterior-root action.
hypotheses: Use the locally convex topological bar construction of SCH11 Remark 3.9, p. 68, with the indicated balanced tensor topology; no identification with the dual of abstract Tor(E,V′) is claimed.
For the locally analytic Levi action assume compact type and Hausdorff homology as in SCH11 p. 82. Kostant cohomology and finite-dimensional duality are the category-O supplier contract.
proofSteps: Form the free/forgetful cotriple resolution and its face and degeneracy maps; apply the topological balanced coinvariant tensor with E and take homology with its quotient topology (SCH11 Remark 3.9, p. 68). The Hausdorff compact-type result and locally analytic Levi action are the argument preceding Corollary 4.9, p. 82. Abstract algebraic Tor on V′ is a different expression and is not substituted for this construction.

For W ⊗ π: N acts on π smoothly; the homology splits as Lie algebra homology of W tensored with the coinvariants of the smooth part, which are the Jacquet module (exactness of J_N, SR.2/jacquet-lemma).
acceptance: For upper N in GL₂ and W=Sym^k(E²), H₀(n,W) has weight (0,k); for lower N⁻ it has weight (k,0). The Levi action must remember which radical was used.

sources.match: Recalls Kohlhaase's definition of the homology groups of a locally analytic representation as the homology of the complex (B_q(G, V) ⊗̃ D(G), ι_K)_q.
For locally algebraic Σ = ψ_alg ⊗ ψ_∞: H_q(n, ψ_alg ⊗ ψ_∞) = H_q(n, ψ_alg) ⊗ ψ_∞ and H_q(N, Σ) = H_q(n, ψ_alg) ⊗ J_N(ψ_∞); Kostant's theorem computes H_q(n, F_λ).

nodes.title: Schraen's spectral sequence for Ext into a parabolic induction
nodes.statement: Let G be split reductive, P = M_P N_P a parabolic subgroup, Σ an admissible locally analytic representation of G and ρ an irreducible locally algebraic representation of M_P (inflated to P). If H_q(N_P, Σ) is Hausdorff for every q ≥ 0, there is a spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = Ext^p_{M_P}(H_q(N_P, Σ), ρ) ⇒ Ext^{p+q}_G(Σ, (Ind_P^G ρ)^an). If moreover the centre Z of G acts on Σ and ρ through a character χ, the same holds with Ext_{M_P,χ} and Ext_{G,χ}.
hypotheses: H_q(N_P, Σ) Hausdorff for all q (holds for locally algebraic Σ and for self-extensions of locally algebraic representations whose restriction to the derived group is locally algebraic).

The source proves derived induction reciprocity for irreducible locally algebraic ρ via the finite-resolution condition (FIN), SCH11 pp. 80–81. The same argument extends to finite successive extensions of such ρ because (FIN) and the required Tor vanishing are extension-stable.

For the Ext notation of LR.1, also require each H_q(N_P,Σ) admissible as an M_P-representation; Hausdorff compact type by itself does not imply admissibility. This holds in the locally algebraic finite-length principal-series applications once the finite-E smooth Jacquet supplier contract is supplied.
proofSteps: Use the (FIN) resolution for ρ′ and Tor_q^{D(P)}(D(G),ρ′)=0 for q>0, SCH11 (4.28)–(4.32), pp. 80–81. This gives derived Frobenius reciprocity for the specified locally algebraic ρ; it is not an assertion of unrestricted flatness over D(P).
Derive: Ext_G(Σ, Ind ρ) = Ext_{D(P)}(ρ′, Σ′), and the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for D(N_P) ⊆ D(P) with Hausdorff homology identifies the E_2-terms (SCH11 §4).
acceptance: For Σ = W ⊗ π locally algebraic, the E_2-terms are Ext^p_{M_P}(H_q(n_P, W) ⊗ J_{N_P}(π), ρ), computed by LR.4/torus-ext when M_P = T.

sources.match: Corollary 4.9 uses the preceding irreducible locally algebraic ρ and compact-type Σ. Hausdorff unipotent homology supplies locally analytic Levi coefficients. The statement here further restricts these to admissible coefficients to fit LR.1’s Ext notation.
Applies Schraen's spectral sequence for G = Res_{K/ℚ_p}GL_n, checking the separatedness hypothesis for π_alg(φ, h) and its self-extensions (locally algebraic after restriction to SL_n(K)).

nodes.title: Vanishing of Ext¹ into inductions from non-adjacent weights
nodes.statement: Let 𝐆 = Res_{L/ℚ_p}GL_n with the notation of Ding, μ ∈ X^+ dominant, π a smooth admissible representation of G = GL_n(L), W := L(μ) ⊗_E π, s ∈ S_n^{|Σ_L|} ≅ W_{Σ_L}, I ⊆ Δ such that s·μ is dominant for the Levi L_I of the standard parabolic P_I, and π_I a finite-length smooth representation of L_I(L). If lg(s) > 1 then (1) Ext^1_G(W, (Ind_{P_I^-}^G L(s·μ)_I ⊗ π_I)^{ℚ_p-an}) = 0 and (2) Ext^1_G(W, F^G_{P_I^-}(L^-(−s·μ), π_I)) = 0. Consequently, push-forward along an injection V ↪ V′ of admissible representations whose cokernel has only constituents of the form F^G_{P_J^-}(L^-(−s·μ), π′) with lg(s) > 1 is an isomorphism on Ext^1_G(W, −).
hypotheses: lg(s) > 1: weights at distance at least two in the Bruhat order from μ do not meet H_0 or H_1(N_I, W).
proofSteps: For the lower unipotent radical of P_I⁻, apply the correctly dualised Kostant formula to W=L(μ)⊗π. The degree-r Levi weights are w·μ for the relevant Levi-dominant representatives of length r. These are the lower-radical weights, not an unadjusted upper-radical formula.

For r ∈ {0, 1} the weights w·μ with lg(w) ≤ 1 differ from s·μ when lg(s) > 1, so Ext^r_{L_I}(H_i(N_I, W), L(s·μ)_I ⊗ π_I) = 0 (LR.1/locally-algebraic-ext); Schraen's spectral sequence (separatedness holds for locally algebraic W) gives (1).
F^G_{P_I}(L^-(−s·μ), π_I) is a subrepresentation of the induction whose quotient has no locally algebraic vectors, so Hom_G(W, quotient) = 0 and (2) follows from (1).

Use the finite-length version of the spectral-sequence target, obtained by dévissage in the locally algebraic inducing representation. For the final push-forward isomorphism, each cokernel factor has no locally algebraic vectors, so Hom_G(W,−)=0 as well as Ext¹_G(W,−)=0; both terms of the long exact sequence are required.
acceptance: For n = 2 there is no s with lg(s) > 1 in a single factor, so the statement has content only for n ≥ 3 or d_L ≥ 2.

sources.match: For lg(s) > 1, Ext^1 from a locally algebraic L(μ) ⊗ π into the parabolic induction of L(s·μ)_I ⊗ π_I and into F^G_{P_I}(L(−s·μ), π_I) vanishes, by Schraen's spectral sequence, Kostant's theorem and Schraen's Proposition 4.7.
Deduces push-forward isomorphisms by dévissage from Lemma 2.26.

sources.locator: §3.1.2, proofs of Lemma 3.5 and Proposition 3.6 and (3.10), pp. 37–38
sources.match: Cites [32, Lem. 2.26] (Ding 2019) for the push-forward isomorphisms used to define (3.10) and to compute Ext^1(π_alg, C(I, s_{i,σ})).

nodes.title: The Orlik–Strauch functor
nodes.statement: Let M ∈ O^p_alg and π_P a smooth admissible representation of L_P(L) over E, inflated to P(L). Choose a finite-dimensional U(p ⊗_{ℚ_p} E)-stable subspace W ⊆ M generating M, so that there is an exact sequence 0 → ker(φ) → U(g ⊗ E) ⊗_{U(p ⊗ E)} W → M → 0; W carries the unique algebraic action of (Res_{L/ℚ_p}P) ×_{ℚ_p} E lifting the p ⊗ E-action, restricted to P(L), and W′ = Hom_E(W, E) the dual action. An element x ⊗ w of U(g ⊗ E) ⊗_E W acts on C^{ℚ_p-an}(G, W′ ⊗ π_P) by f ↦ (g ↦ (x·f)(g)(w)) with the derived action of LR.0/derived-lie-action, and this descends to U(g ⊗ E) ⊗_{U(p ⊗ E)} W on the induction. The Orlik–Strauch representation is F^G_P(M, π_P) := (Ind_{P(L)}^{G(L)} W′ ⊗_E π_P)^{ker(φ)}, the closed subspace of the locally ℚ_p-analytic induction (LR.4/locally-analytic-induction) annihilated by ker(φ). It is a closed G(L)-stable subspace, independent of the choice of W, admissible, strongly admissible when π_P has finite length, and very strongly admissible when π_P is. Write F^G_P(M) := F^G_P(M, 1).
hypotheses: 𝐆 split connected reductive over L, B = TN ⊆ P = L_P N_P a Borel and a parabolic (standard or opposite), E/ℚ_p finite splitting L; O^p_alg is the category of the gap 'Category O and Kostant homology' for the ℚ_p-Lie algebra g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E = ∏_σ g_σ: finitely generated U(g ⊗ E)-modules, direct sums of simple algebraic U(l_P ⊗ E)-modules, locally finite for n_P ⊗ E.

The theory of Orlik–Strauch is for locally L-analytic representations of G(L); Breuil extends it to the locally ℚ_p-analytic setting used here (Breuil states p > 3 if G has factors not of type A; no restriction for GL_n).
proofSteps: The derived U(g ⊗ E)-action on C^an(G, W′ ⊗ π_P) and the pairing with W give continuous maps x ⊗ w : C^an(G, W′ ⊗ π_P) → C^an(G, π_P); on the induction they factor through U(g ⊗ E) ⊗_{U(p ⊗ E)} W (BR16 Lemma 2.1), so the annihilator of ker(φ) is defined and closed.
It is G-stable because the left-derivative action (5) of BR16 commutes with right translation.

Independence of W and admissibility follow from the analytic norm-completion presentations of OS15 §4 and BR16 Theorem 2.3(i), with the closed annihilator relations in the completed induction dual. BR16 Lemma 2.2 alone gives only a dense algebraic image. Very strong admissibility follows by the closed subrepresentation of the induction, applying EMJ2 Proposition 2.1.2 to W′⊗π_P via the finite-dimensional algebraic tensor identity.
acceptance: For a generalised Verma module M = U(g ⊗ E) ⊗_{U(p ⊗ E)} W one has ker(φ) = 0 and F^G_P(M, π_P) = (Ind_P^G W′ ⊗ π_P)^an.
