nodes.title: Exactness and functoriality of the Orlik–Strauch functor
nodes.statement: F^G_P : O^p_alg × Rep^{∞,adm}_E(L_P(L)) → Rep^a_E(G(L)) is a bifunctor, contravariant in M and covariant in π_P, and exact in each argument.
hypotheses: 𝐆 split connected reductive over L, B = TN ⊆ P = L_P N_P a Borel and a parabolic (standard or opposite), E/ℚ_p finite splitting L; O^p_alg is the category of the gap 'Category O and Kostant homology' for the ℚ_p-Lie algebra g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E = ∏_σ g_σ: finitely generated U(g ⊗ E)-modules, direct sums of simple algebraic U(l_P ⊗ E)-modules, locally finite for n_P ⊗ E.
proofSteps: For exactness in M, choose compatible finite-dimensional P-stable generating spaces and diagrams of generalised Verma presentations. Pass to the analytic norm completions where the flatness theorem applies, prove exactness there, and recover the locally analytic representations by the compact-type duality (OS15 Proposition 4.2, pp. 18–19; BR16 Theorem 2.3(ii)). This does not assert blanket flatness of D(G) over D(g,P) on arbitrary modules.

For the smooth variable, use an analytic section on compact charts and the presentation with analytic-function factor and algebraic smooth tensor factor; exactness of the latter preserves the finite differential-equation kernel (OS15 Proposition 4.9(a), p. 22). Dualise with strictness of the admissible category.
acceptance: Applied to 0 → K → M^-(−λ) → L^-(−λ) → 0 it gives 0 → F(L^-(−λ), χ) → PS → F(K, χ) → 0.

sources.locator: Introduction, main theorem (i)–(ii), p. 3; §4, Proposition 4.9(a), p. 22
sources.match: F^G_P is functorial in both arguments, contravariant in M and covariant in V, and exact in both arguments.
The construction (M, π_P) ↦ F^G_P(M, π_P) is functorial and exact in both arguments in the locally ℚ_p-analytic setting.
Exactness in the category-O variable is proved through generating-space presentations and analytic completions.

nodes.title: Transitivity of the Orlik–Strauch functor along parabolics
nodes.statement: If Q ⊇ P are parabolic subgroups and M ∈ O^q_alg ⊆ O^p_alg, then F^G_P(M, π_P) ≅ F^G_Q(M, i^{L_Q}_{P ∩ L_Q}(π_P)) for every smooth admissible π_P, where i^{L_Q}_{P∩L_Q}(π_P) = (Ind_{P(L) ∩ L_Q(L)}^{L_Q(L)} π_P)^∞ is smooth parabolic induction (of finite length when π_P is).
hypotheses: 𝐆 split connected reductive over L, B = TN ⊆ P = L_P N_P a Borel and a parabolic (standard or opposite), E/ℚ_p finite splitting L; O^p_alg is the category of the gap 'Category O and Kostant homology' for the ℚ_p-Lie algebra g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E = ∏_σ g_σ: finitely generated U(g ⊗ E)-modules, direct sums of simple algebraic U(l_P ⊗ E)-modules, locally finite for n_P ⊗ E.
proofSteps: For M ∈ O^q_alg one may take W ⊆ M stable under q, so the induction from P factors through Q by transitivity of locally analytic induction (LR.4/locally-analytic-induction); the condition 'killed by ker φ' only involves the algebraic part along L_Q, and on the smooth part the inner induction is the smooth one.
acceptance: For P = B, Q = G and M = L(λ)^∨ finite-dimensional: F^G_B(L(λ)^∨, χ) ≅ L(λ) ⊗ (Ind_B^G χ)^∞.

sources.locator: Introduction, main theorem (iii), p. 3; §4, Proposition 4.9(b), p. 22
sources.match: For M ∈ O^q_alg, F^G_P(M, V) = F^G_Q(M, i^{L_Q}_{L_P}(V)) with smooth induction in the middle.
The same identity in the locally ℚ_p-analytic setting, by the proof of OS Proposition 4.10(b).

nodes.title: The Orlik–Strauch irreducibility theorem
nodes.statement: Let M ∈ O^p_alg and π_P a smooth admissible representation of L_P(L). Then F^G_P(M, π_P) is topologically irreducible if and only if M is simple and, for the parabolic Q ⊇ P maximal for M (the largest Q with M ∈ O^q_alg), the smooth induction i^{L_Q}_{P∩L_Q}(π_P) is irreducible. In particular, for M simple with maximal parabolic P and π_P irreducible, F^G_P(M, π_P) is irreducible. Moreover F^G_{Q_1}(M_1, π_{Q_1}) ≅ F^G_{Q_2}(M_2, π_{Q_2}) for simple M_i with maximal parabolics Q_i and finite-length π_{Q_i} if and only if M_1 ≅ M_2 (hence Q_1 = Q_2) and π_{Q_1} ≅ π_{Q_2}. For this locally ℚ_p-analytic form assume p > 3 if 𝐆 has any factors not of type A, as in BR16 §1, p. 6; there is no restriction for GL_n. In the original locally L-analytic OS15 theorem the sharper bounds are p > 2 for B,C,F₄ and p > 3 for G₂.
hypotheses: 𝐆 split connected reductive over L, B = TN ⊆ P = L_P N_P a Borel and a parabolic (standard or opposite), E/ℚ_p finite splitting L; O^p_alg is the category of the gap 'Category O and Kostant homology' for the ℚ_p-Lie algebra g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E = ∏_σ g_σ: finitely generated U(g ⊗ E)-modules, direct sums of simple algebraic U(l_P ⊗ E)-modules, locally finite for n_P ⊗ E.

The stated ℚ_p-analytic result uses Breuil’s conservative p>3 assumption for every non-A factor. The sharper locally L-analytic bounds are recorded separately and are not silently promoted to this extension.
proofSteps: Reduce by LR.5/orlik-strauch-transitivity to P maximal for M.

OS15 Theorem 5.3: for M simple with P maximal, D(G_0) ⊗_{D(g, P_0)} M is a simple D(G_0)-module for a compact open G_0, via a careful analysis of the D(g, P_0)-module structure and Jantzen-type arguments; then irreducibility under G follows (OS15 Theorems 5.3, 5.8).
Uniqueness (BR16 Cor. 2.7): the n-invariants of the dual recover the highest weight of M and π_Q′ (BR16 Proposition 2.4).
acceptance: For GL_2(ℚ_p), λ dominant and s the simple reflection, F^G_{B^-}(L^-(−s·λ), χ) is irreducible: the 'non-locally-algebraic' constituent of PS(z^λ χ).

sources.locator: Introduction, main theorem (iv) and the remark after it, pp. 3–4; §5, Assumption 5.1, p. 25; Theorem 5.8, p. 37
sources.match: F^G_P(M, V) is topologically irreducible iff M is simple and the smooth induction to the maximal parabolic for M is irreducible, under p > 2 for types B, C, F_4 and p > 3 for G_2; the authors know no counterexample for small p.
In the ℚ_p-analytic setting, F^G_P(M, π_P) is irreducible for M simple, P maximal for M and π_P irreducible; F^G_{Q_1}(M_1, π_{Q_1}) ≅ F^G_{Q_2}(M_2, π_{Q_2}) iff M_1 ≅ M_2 and π_{Q_1} ≅ π_{Q_2}.

nodes.title: Jordan–Hölder series and socles of Orlik–Strauch representations
nodes.statement: (1) For M ∈ O^p_alg with Jordan–Hölder series M = M^0 ⊋ M^1 ⊋ … ⊋ M^{r+1} = 0 there is a filtration of F^G_P(M, π_P) by closed subrepresentations with graded pieces F^G_P(M^i/M^{i+1}, π_P); refining it gives a Jordan–Hölder series whose irreducible constituents are the F^G_{Q_i}(M^i/M^{i+1}, π′) for π′ running over the constituents of i^{L_{Q_i}}_{P∩L_{Q_i}}(π_P), Q_i the maximal parabolic of M^i/M^{i+1}; the multiplicity of F^G_Q(L, π_Q) is [M : L]·[i^{L_Q}_{P∩L_Q}(π_P) : π_Q]. (2) (Socle.) For W an irreducible algebraic representation of L_P of highest weight λ_W, M the simple quotient of U(g ⊗ E) ⊗_{U(p ⊗ E)} W with maximal parabolic Q ⊇ P, and π_P of finite length: soc_G F^G_P(M, π_P) = F^G_Q(M, soc_{L_Q} i^{L_Q}_{P∩L_Q} π_P) = soc_G (Ind_P^G W′ ⊗ π_P)^an. (3) H^0(N_Q(L), F^G_Q(M, π_Q)′) ≅ W(Q) ⊗_E π_Q′ as L_Q(L)-representations, W(Q) the irreducible algebraic representation of L_Q of highest weight λ_W. (4) (Full faithfulness, L-analytic case.) For M_1, M_2 ∈ O^p_alg, Hom_{O^p_alg}(M_1, M_2) → Hom_G(F^G_P(M_2), F^G_P(M_1)) is bijective.
hypotheses: 𝐆 split connected reductive over L, B = TN ⊆ P = L_P N_P a Borel and a parabolic (standard or opposite), E/ℚ_p finite splitting L; O^p_alg is the category of the gap 'Category O and Kostant homology' for the ℚ_p-Lie algebra g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E = ∏_σ g_σ: finitely generated U(g ⊗ E)-modules, direct sums of simple algebraic U(l_P ⊗ E)-modules, locally finite for n_P ⊗ E.

Use the residue-characteristic hypotheses of LR.5/orlik-strauch-irreducibility. In (1), require π_P finite length so that the refined series is finite. Part (4) is only the locally L-analytic result with trivial smooth argument, OR19 Theorem 1, p. 2; no ℚ_p-analytic or arbitrary-smooth-argument extension is used downstream.
proofSteps: (1): exactness (LR.5/orlik-strauch-exactness) turns a Jordan–Hölder series of M into a filtration; each graded piece is F^G_P(M_i, π_P) with M_i simple, which by transitivity equals F^G_{Q_i}(M_i, i(π_P)), and exactness in the second argument plus irreducibility (LR.5/orlik-strauch-irreducibility) refine it.

(2)–(3): BR16 Proposition 2.4 computes N_Q-invariants of the dual; an irreducible subrepresentation F^G_Q(M, π_Q) gives a quotient W(Q) ⊗ π_Q′ of W(Q) ⊗ i(π_P)′, so π_Q lies in the socle of the smooth induction; constituents with other M̃ are excluded by comparing torus weights of highest weight vectors (BR16 Cor. 2.5).
(4): Orlik's Casselman–Jacquet-type functor G^G_P(U) = colim_k H^0(u_P^k, U′) is almost a section of F^G_P (OR19).
acceptance: For GL_2(ℚ_p) and λ dominant: PS(z^λ χ) has length 2 when (Ind χ)^∞ is irreducible, with socle L(λ) ⊗ (Ind χ)^∞ and cosocle F(L^-(−s·λ), χ).

sources.match: From a Jordan–Hölder series of M one gets a filtration of F^G_P(M, V) with graded pieces F^G_P(M^i/M^{i+1}, V); refining gives a Jordan–Hölder series with constituents F^G_{Q_i}(M^i/M^{i+1}, v^{Q_i}_Q).

sources.locator: §2, Proposition 2.4 and Corollary 2.5 with proof, pp. 10–12
sources.match: Computes H^0(N_Q, F^G_Q(M, π_Q)′) = W(Q) ⊗ π_Q′ and the socle of F^G_P(M, π_P) and of the induction.
For M_1, M_2 ∈ O^p_alg the map Hom(M_1, M_2) → Hom_G(F^G_P(M_2), F^G_P(M_1)) is bijective.
Uses the structure of Verma modules and the Orlik–Strauch theory to list the irreducible constituents of F^{G_p}_{B_p}(δ_{R,w}).

nodes.title: Orlik–Strauch theory for products of groups over different fields
nodes.statement: Let G = G_1(L_1) × G_2(L_2) with 𝐆_i split reductive over finite extensions L_i/ℚ_p (not necessarily equal) and E splitting L_1 and L_2. With g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E = (g_1 ⊗ E) × (g_2 ⊗ E), parabolics P = P_1 × P_2 and O^p_alg defined for g ⊗ E, the constructions and results of LR.5 hold for locally ℚ_p-analytic representations of G over E: F^G_P(M_1 ⊠ M_2, π_1 ⊠ π_2) ≅ F^{G_1}_{P_1}(M_1, π_1) ⊗̂_E F^{G_2}_{P_2}(M_2, π_2); the exactness, transitivity, irreducibility, Jordan–Hölder and socle statements. The product versions of LR.6 are treated after those adjunctions are defined; they are not prerequisites for this LR.5 target.
hypotheses: 𝐆 split connected reductive over L, B = TN ⊆ P = L_P N_P a Borel and a parabolic (standard or opposite), E/ℚ_p finite splitting L; O^p_alg is the category of the gap 'Category O and Kostant homology' for the ℚ_p-Lie algebra g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E = ∏_σ g_σ: finitely generated U(g ⊗ E)-modules, direct sums of simple algebraic U(l_P ⊗ E)-modules, locally finite for n_P ⊗ E.
This is a genuine proof obligation: the source asserts the extension after an examination of the proofs and gives no argument.
proofSteps: Enveloping algebras and root data factor over the groups and embeddings. Simple category-O objects are external tensor products of simple objects; arbitrary finite-length objects need not be pure tensors and are handled by finite extensions and exactness.

For M = M_1 ⊠ M_2 choose W = W_1 ⊠ W_2; the induction from P_1 × P_2 is the completed tensor product of the inductions (LR.0/completed-external-tensor), and ker(φ) = ker(φ_1) ⊗ U_2 + U_1 ⊗ ker(φ_2), giving the tensor product formula.

For simple objects, run the irreducibility and invariant-weight arguments factor by factor, using the product Bruhat and Iwasawa decompositions and compact-open analytic distribution presentations. Extend the finite-length statements using the exact functors. LR.6 adjunctions require their own later product argument, as indicated in BHS Remark 5.1.2; they are not used here.
acceptance: For G_2 = 1 the statement is the theory of LR.5 for G_1(L_1).

sources.match: The Orlik–Strauch results used are stated only for G(K) with G split reductive over K and L splitting K, but are needed for products G_1(K_1) × G_2(K_2) with K_1 ≠ K_2; an examination of the proofs (and of the results of Orlik–Strauch and Emerton on which they rely) shows that they extend when L splits K_1 and K_2.
Writes F^{G_p}_{B_p}{L(−μ), ε_sm δ^{-1}_{B_p}} ≃ ⊗̂_{v∈S_p} F^{G_v}_{B_v}{L(−μ_v), ε_sm δ^{-1}_{B_v}} for the product group G_p = ∏_v G_v.

nodes.title: The rigid character variety of an abelian locally analytic group
nodes.statement: Let Z be an abelian locally F-analytic group which is topologically finitely generated, equivalently Z ≅ Z_0 × Λ with Z_0 compact open (the maximal compact subgroup) and Λ ≅ ℤ^r discrete. The functor Ẑ on rigid analytic spaces X over F, Ẑ(X) = characters Z → O(X)^× that are locally analytic over every affinoid open of X, is representable by a strictly quasi-Stein rigid space, Ẑ ≅ Ẑ_0 × 𝔾_m^{r,an}. Its ring of functions C^an(Ẑ, E) is a Fréchet–Stein algebra, and integration against characters gives a continuous injective algebra map D(Z, E) → C^an(Ẑ, E) with dense image, an isomorphism when Z is compact (the Mellin transform). For T = 𝐓(L) a split torus, T̂ parametrises the locally ℚ_p-analytic characters of T, and a point δ ∈ T̂(E) has weight dδ ∈ ∏_σ t_σ^*.
hypotheses: Z topologically finitely generated (true for the centre of a Levi of a reductive group and for T = 𝐓(L)).

For L ≠ ℚ_p and F = L the compact part needs the Lubin–Tate Fourier theory of Schneider–Teitelbaum; the ℚ_p-analytic case used here reduces to products of ℤ_p-characters (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L3).
proofSteps: Decompose Z=Z_0×Λ (EM17 Proposition 6.4.1, p. 124). The discrete factor has character variety 𝔾_m^r. For compact Z_0 import the compact character-space/Mellin construction; after a finite coefficient extension splitting the finite torsion characters it is a finite disjoint union of open polydiscs in the ℚ_p-analytic case. Descend to E if that splitting is not already present.

Use the quasi-Stein affinoid exhaustion with noetherian Banach function algebras and flat restriction maps of EM17 Propositions 6.4.5–6.4.6, pp. 126–127, to obtain the Fréchet–Stein algebra. Theorems A and B alone are not a substitute for these noetherian and flatness checks. The adic supplier requires its stated rigid/adic comparison contract.
D(Z_0, E) ≅ C^an(Ẑ_0, E) by the Mellin transform (L3/mellin-frechet-isomorphism); D(Λ, E) = E[Λ] is dense in O(𝔾_m^r) (EM17 Prop. 6.4.6).
acceptance: For Z = ℤ_p (F = ℚ_p), Ẑ is the open unit disc via χ ↦ χ(1) − 1, and D(ℤ_p, E) ≅ O(open disc) (Amice).

uses.how: the finite slope part is defined as Z^+-equivariant maps from C^an(Ẑ, E)
essentially admissible representations are coadmissible over C^an(Ẑ, E) ⊗̂ D(H, E)
the dual of J_B(Π) is a coherent sheaf on T̂; eigenvarieties are schematic supports
characters δ = w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε) as E[ε]-points of T̂

sources.locator: §6.4, Proposition 6.4.1, p. 124; Definition 6.4.2, p. 125; Propositions 6.4.5–6.4.6, pp. 126–127
sources.match: Characterises topologically finitely generated abelian locally analytic groups as Z_0 × Λ, defines the character functor Ẑ, proves it is representable by a strictly quasi-Stein rigid space, and gives the dense injection D_la(Z, K) → C^an(Ẑ, K), an isomorphism for compact Z (via Schneider–Teitelbaum's Fourier theory).

nodes.title: Essentially admissible representations
nodes.statement: Let G be a locally analytic group whose centre Z is topologically finitely generated, and H a compact open subgroup. A locally analytic representation V of G on a space of compact type is essentially admissible if the Z-action satisfies the equivalent conditions of Emerton (it extends to a separately continuous C^an(Ẑ, E)-module structure; equivalently V is a union of an increasing sequence of Z-stable BH-subspaces) and, for one (equivalently every) H, the dual V′_b is a coadmissible module over the Fréchet–Stein algebra C^an(Ẑ, E) ⊗̂_E D(H, E). Every admissible representation is essentially admissible; Rep^es_E(G) is abelian.
hypotheses: Compact type; topologically finitely generated centre.
proofSteps: The C^an(Ẑ, E)-structure, if it exists, is unique (EM17 Prop. 6.4.7).

Admissible ⇒ essentially admissible: V is the union of the Z-stable images of V_{H_n-an}, so condition (iii) of EM17 Prop. 6.4.7 holds, and the dual is coadmissible already over D(H, E) (EM17 Prop. 6.4.10).
acceptance: Every character is essentially admissible; for G=ℤ discrete the universal character family O(𝔾_m^an)′ is essentially admissible and infinite-dimensional, hence not admissible.

uses.how: J_P takes essentially admissible G-representations to essentially admissible M-representations
the dual of J_B(Π^an) is a coherent sheaf on T̂ whose support is an eigenvariety

api.name: IsEssentiallyAdmissible
api.statement: The Z-action extends to C^an(Ẑ, E) and V′ is coadmissible over C^an(Ẑ, E) ⊗̂ D(H, E).

api.name: IsAdmissible.isEssentiallyAdmissible
api.statement: Admissible ⇒ essentially admissible.

api.name: essentiallyAdmissible_coherentSheaf
api.statement: V ↦ V′ identifies Rep^es_E(G) with coadmissible C^an(Ẑ) ⊗̂ D(H)-modules with compatible G-action, i.e. G-equivariant coherent sheaves on Ẑ with D(H)-structure.

api.name: essentiallyAdmissible_abelian
api.statement: Rep^es_E(G) is an abelian category with strict morphisms.

tests.name: essAdm_character
tests.statement: Under this roadmap’s contragredient left-dual convention, the dual of the character χ is the skyscraper at χ^{-1} in Ẑ. If the geometric parameter is labelled by χ instead, the inversion automorphism of Ẑ must be applied explicitly.

tests.name: essAdm_admissible
tests.statement: Every admissible representation is essentially admissible (EM17 Prop. 6.4.10).

tests.name: essAdm_not_admissible
tests.statement: Take G=Z=ℤ discrete, H={1} and V=O(𝔾_m^an)′_b with the contragredient universal character action. It is essentially admissible since its dual is the regular rank-one O(𝔾_m^an)-module. Admissibility for H={1} would force its dual to be finite-dimensional over E, which it is not (EM17 p. 129). Non-finite-generation by itself would not disprove coadmissibility for a general nontrivial H.

tests.name: essAdm_zero
tests.statement: The zero representation is essentially admissible.

sources.match: Gives three equivalent conditions for the Z-action to extend to C^an(Ẑ, K), defines essentially admissible representations by coadmissibility of the dual over C^an(Ẑ, K) ⊗̂ D(H, K), and shows admissible representations are essentially admissible.
The Jacquet module of an admissible representation is essentially admissible but need not be admissible.

nodes.title: The finite slope part of a Z^+-representation
nodes.statement: Let Z be a topologically finitely generated abelian locally analytic group and Z^+ ⊆ Z a submonoid containing a compact open subgroup Z_0 and generating Z as a group. For V a Hausdorff locally convex representation of Z^+ of compact type, the finite slope part is V_fs := L_{b,Z^+}(C^an(Ẑ, E), V), the Z^+-equivariant continuous linear maps (Z acts on C^an(Ẑ, E) through Z ⊆ C^an(Ẑ, E)^×), with the strong topology; evaluation at 1 gives a Z^+-equivariant map V_fs → V. V ↦ V_fs is right adjoint to the forgetful functor from locally analytic Z-representations (of compact type, with the C^an(Ẑ)-structure) to topological Z^+-representations.
hypotheses: Z^+ generates Z as a group and contains a compact open subgroup.
proofSteps: C^an(Ẑ, E) is a locally analytic Z-representation on which Z acts invertibly; maps out of it equivariant for Z^+ are the universal way to make the Z^+-action invertible and locally analytic.

For U in Rep^{zla.c}(Z), its Z-stable BH exhaustion gives the continuous O(Ẑ)-module structure. Use this structure to extend the orbit functional associated with a Z^+-map U→V, obtaining a unique map U→V_fs. This argument requires Rep^{zla.c}, not merely a compact-type locally analytic action.
acceptance: For V ∈ Rep^{zla.c}(Z) and Z^+=Z, evaluation identifies V_fs with V. Here zla means an exhaustive increasing sequence of Z-stable BH subspaces, equivalently the required O(Ẑ)-module structure.

uses.how: J_P(V) := (V^{N_0})_fs with Z^+ = Z_M^+ acting by Hecke operators
the finite slope part of completed cohomology at an eigenvariety point

api.name: finiteSlopePart
api.statement: V_fs := L_{b,Z^+}(C^an(Ẑ, E), V).

api.name: finiteSlopePart_eval
api.statement: The Z^+-equivariant map V_fs → V, evaluation at 1 ∈ C^an(Ẑ, E).

api.name: finiteSlopePart_adjunction
api.statement: Hom_Z(U,V_fs) ≅ Hom_{Z^+}(U,V) for U ∈ Rep^{zla.c}(Z), with a Z-stable BH exhaustion and the resulting O(Ẑ)-structure.

api.name: finiteSlopePart_leftExact
api.statement: V ↦ V_fs is left exact and additive.

api.name: finiteSlopePart_of_la
api.statement: If Z^+=Z and V ∈ Rep^{zla.c}(Z), then evaluation V_fs→V is an isomorphism.

tests.name: finiteSlopePart_Z
tests.statement: For Z^+=Z and V ∈ Rep^{zla.c}(Z), V_fs=V; the stable BH exhaustion is part of the test data.

tests.name: finiteSlopePart_zero_operator
tests.statement: If z ∈ Z^+ acts by 0 on V then V_fs = 0, since z acts invertibly on C^an(Ẑ, E).

tests.name: finiteSlopePart_finiteDim

sources.locator: §3.2, Definition 3.2.1 and the following discussion, p. 796
sources.match: Defines V_fs := L_{b,Z^+}(C^an(Ẑ, K), V) for V in Rep^{top.c}(Z^+), constructing the right adjoint of the forgetful functor from Rep^{zla.c}(Z).

sources.locator: §3.2, Propositions 3.2.4–3.2.15 (cited in the construction of J_P), pp. 797–803
sources.match: Establishes the properties of the finite slope part used to define J_P.

nodes.title: Emerton's locally analytic Jacquet functor
nodes.statement: Let G be split reductive (or any p-adic reductive group), P = M N a parabolic with Levi M, Z_M the centre of M, N_0 ⊆ N a compact open subgroup, and M^+ := {m ∈ M : m N_0 m^{-1} ⊆ N_0}, Z_M^+ := Z_M ∩ M^+. For a locally analytic representation V of P of compact type, the N_0-invariants V^{N_0} carry the Hecke action of M^+ by π_{N_0,m}(v) = [N_0:mN_0m^{-1}]^{-1} Σ_{n ∈ N_0/mN_0m^{-1}} nm·v, and the Jacquet–Emerton module is J_P(V) := (V^{N_0})_fs (the finite slope part for Z_M^+), a locally analytic representation of M (with its Z_M-action locally analytic). J_P is the right adjoint, twisted by the modulus character δ_P, of C^sm_c(N, −): for U in Rep^{zla.c}(M), Hom_P(C^sm_c(N, U), V) ≅ Hom_M(U(δ_P), J_P(V)). Composing with restriction gives J_P : Rep^{la.c}(G) → Rep^{zla.c}(M). It is left exact, independent of N_0, and agrees with the smooth Jacquet module (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2/jacquet-module) on admissible smooth representations.
hypotheses: Compact-type representations; the Hecke operators require N_0 compact open and M^+ the contracting monoid.
δ_P(m)=|det(Ad(m)|n)|_L. For m contracting N_0, δ_P(m)=[N_0:mN_0m^{-1}]^{-1}. All Jacquet modules in this roadmap use Emerton’s averaged action.
proofSteps: V^{N_0} is a closed Z_M^+-stable subspace with Hecke action (EMJ1 §3.3); its finite slope part is defined by LR.6/finite-slope-part.
Independence of N_0 and the adjunction (0.4) are EMJ1 §3.4–3.5 (Theorem 3.5.6).

Agreement with the smooth Jacquet module: for admissible smooth V, Jacquet's lemma identifies V^{N_0} with finite slope Hecke action and its finite slope part with V_N (SR.2/jacquet-lemma, SR.2/jacquet-invariants).
acceptance: For V = π smooth admissible, J_P(π) = π_N, the smooth Jacquet module (unnormalised).

uses.how: Hom_{T(K)}(z^{s_{i,σ}·λ} w(φ)ηδ_B, J_B(C(I, s_{i,σ}))) ≅ E
J_{B_p}(Π̂^an) and its dual coherent sheaf on T̂, whose support defines the eigenvariety
the Jacquet–Emerton/Orlik–Strauch compatibility (3.10)

api.name: jacquetEmerton_adjunction

api.name: jacquetEmerton_smooth

tests.statement: For GL_2(ℚ_p) and W = Sym^k(E²), J_B(W) = W^{N} = the highest-weight line, the character z^{(k,0)} of T (EMJ1 Proposition 4.3.6 with X = 1).

tests.name: jacquetEmerton_Hecke_average_GL2
tests.statement: Let G=GL₂(ℚ_p), P=B upper triangular, N_0=N(ℤ_p), m=diag(p,1), V=E trivial. The index is p, the sum is p·id and π_{N_0,m}=id. An unaveraged sum would twist J_B(1) and fail J_B(1)=1.

sources.match: C^sm_c(N, −) has a right adjoint; J_P is defined as this right adjoint twisted by the modulus character, with the adjunction isomorphism (0.4); J_P is left exact and additive and agrees with the usual Jacquet module on admissible smooth representations.
Defines J_P(V) := (V^{N_0})_fs for V in Rep^{la.c}(P).
The Hecke operator is the Haar average of mv, with inverse-index factor; evaluation is M_0N_0-equivariant.

nodes.title: Admissibility and computations of Emerton's Jacquet modules
nodes.statement: (1) J_P takes essentially admissible G-representations to essentially admissible M-representations, and J_P : Rep^es_E(G) → Rep^es_E(M) is additive and left exact. (2) If W is a finite-dimensional algebraic representation of G with B = End_G(W) and X an admissible smooth representation of G over B, then J_P(X ⊗_B W) ≅ X_N ⊗_B W^N, with X_N the smooth Jacquet module and W^N = W^{N_0} the N-invariants (locally algebraic representations have locally algebraic Jacquet modules). (3) For G quasi-split and P a Borel: a topologically irreducible very strongly admissible V with J_P(V) ≠ 0 is a subquotient of the locally analytic induction of a locally analytic character of the torus; and an admissible representation of finite length with very strongly admissible constituents has finite-dimensional J_P(V). (4) For Π admissible Banach, J_B(Π^la)′ is a coadmissible C^an(T̂, E)-module, i.e. a coherent sheaf on T̂ with a compatible T-action.
proofSteps: (1) is EMJ1 Theorem 4.2.32: compactness of Hecke operators on the BH-subspaces V_{H-an} (EMJ1 §2) gives coadmissibility of the dual of the finite slope part.
(2) is EMJ1 Proposition 4.3.6, from Jacquet's lemma for X (SR.2/jacquet-lemma) and W^{N_0} = W^N.
(3) is EMJ1 Theorem 0.6 and EMJ2 Corollaries 0.14–0.15, via the adjunction LR.6/emerton-adjunction.
(4) combines (1) for P = B with LR.6/essentially-admissible's description of essentially admissible T-representations as coherent sheaves on T̂.
acceptance: For π_alg = I_sm(φ) ⊗ L(λ) of GL_n(L) with φ generic, J_B(π_alg) ≅ J_N(I_sm(φ)) ⊗ L(λ)^N is a direct sum of n! distinct characters of T (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2/principal-series-jacquet and genericity).

sources.match: J_P takes essentially admissible representations to essentially admissible ones, giving an additive left exact functor Rep^es(G) → Rep^es(M).
For X admissible smooth and W algebraic, J_P(X⊗_B W) ≅ X_N⊗_B W^N, using invariants of W, not its coinvariants.
For G quasi-split and P Borel, an irreducible admissible representation embedding in an admissible Banach representation with J_P(V) ≠ 0 is a subquotient of a locally analytic principal series.

Under the same hypotheses such V is a quotient of I_P^G(U) for a finite-dimensional U, and finite-length admissible representations with very strongly admissible constituents have finite-dimensional J_P.
Uses that the continuous dual of J_{B_p}(Π̂^an) is a coherent sheaf on T̂_p.

nodes.title: Emerton's closed induction I_P^G
nodes.statement: For U ∈ Rep^{zla.c}(M) (a locally analytic representation of M of compact type on which Z_M acts locally analytically), Lemma 0.3 of Emerton gives a closed M-equivariant embedding U(δ_P) → J_P((Ind_{P^-}^G U)^an) (here P^- is opposite to P, and the induction is the locally analytic induction of LR.4). Composing with the canonical lifting J_P(Ind U) → Ind U, the closed G-subrepresentation I_{P^-}^G(U) ⊆ (Ind_{P^-}^G U)^an generated by the image is Emerton's closed induction. Equivalently it is the closed G-subrepresentation generated by the functions supported on the big cell P^- N with locally constant compactly supported restriction to N (EMJ2 Lemma 2.8.3). When G is quasi-split and P is a Borel, the inclusion induces J_P(I_{P^-}^G(U)) ≅ J_P((Ind_{P^-}^G U)^an).
hypotheses: The conventions match Ding: induction from P^- = B^- of characters of T, Jacquet module for P = B.
U ∈ Rep^{zla.c}(M): the centre has a stable BH exhaustion, not just a locally analytic action. The Jacquet equality from EMJ2 Corollary 5.1.4 is only claimed for quasi-split G and a Borel P.
proofSteps: EMJ2 Lemma 0.3 provides the closed embedding; its image lifts canonically into Ind U (LR.6/jacquet-emerton-functor), and the closed span of its G-translates is I(U).
Lemma 2.8.3 identifies the generators with smooth compactly supported functions on the big cell; Corollary 5.1.4 computes J_P of I(U).
acceptance: For U = z^λ χ_sm with λ dominant, I_{B^-}^G(U) is the locally algebraic subrepresentation (Ind χ_sm)^∞ ⊗ L(λ) of the principal series.

uses.how: ζ_w(ψ) = I_{B^-}(w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε)) as self-extensions and extensions of π_alg by subrepresentations of PS_1
the source of the adjunction

api.name: closedInduction
api.statement: I_{P^-}^G(U) ⊆ (Ind_{P^-}^G U)^an, a closed subrepresentation.

api.name: closedInduction_le
api.statement: I_{P^-}^G(U) ⊆ (Ind_{P^-}^G U)^an; the inclusion is in general proper (for U smooth, I(U) is the smooth induction).

api.name: closedInduction_jacquet
api.statement: For quasi-split G and Borel P, J_P(I(U)) ≅ J_P((Ind U)^an).

api.name: closedInduction_functorial
api.statement: Functorial in U.

api.name: closedInduction_lalg
api.statement: For U = χ_sm z^λ with λ dominant, I(U) = (Ind χ_sm)^∞ ⊗ L(λ).

api.name: closedInduction_deformed
api.statement: For a deformed character U = δ(1 + ψε), I(U) is an E[ε]-module and, for δ = w(φ)ηz^λ, ψ = ψ_1 + ψ_0 ∘ det with ψ_1 smooth: I(U) ≅ (Ind w(φ)η(1 + ψ_1ε))^∞ ⊗ L(λ) ⊗ (1 + εψ_0 ∘ det).

tests.statement: For U a smooth character χ, I_{B^-}^G(χ) = (Ind_{B^-}^G χ)^∞, the smooth induction, a proper subspace of the locally analytic one.

In contrast I(z^λχ_sm) is the proper locally algebraic subrepresentation. Non-dominance does not imply a proper closed induction.

sources.locator: Introduction, the definition of I_P^G(U) and Lemma 0.3, p. 2
sources.match: Defines I_P^G(U) as the closed G-subrepresentation of Ind_P^G U generated by the image of U under the canonical lifting of J_P(Ind_P^G U), using the closed embedding U(δ) → J_P(Ind_P^G U).
Describes I_P^G(U) as the closed G-subrepresentation generated by the image of the closed embedding (2.8.2) of compactly supported smooth functions on the big cell.
For quasi-split G and a Borel, the closed induction has the same Jacquet module as the full induction; no arbitrary-parabolic version is inferred.
Uses I_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}(δ) for characters δ and for deformed characters δ(1 + ψε), e.g. I(w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε)) ≅ (Ind w(φ)η(1 + ψ_1ε))^sm ⊗ L(λ) ⊗ (1 + εψ_0 ∘ det).

nodes.title: Balanced maps into a Jacquet module
nodes.statement: Let U ∈ Rep^{zla.c}(M) and V a locally analytic representation of G. A continuous M-equivariant map U(δ_P) → J_P(V) is balanced if the kernel of the induced (g, P)-map U(g) ⊗_{U(p)} U → U(g) ⊗_{U(p)} J_P(V) → V (via the canonical lifting) contains the kernel of the natural map U(g) ⊗_{U(p)} U → (Ind_{P^-}^G U)^an. L_M(U(δ_P), J_P(V))^bal denotes the subspace of balanced maps; it depends on J_P(V) as the Jacquet module of V, contains the image of Hom_G(I_{P^-}^G(U), V), and the balanced condition does not depend on N_0. U is allowable if, for all finite-dimensional algebraic M-representations W_1, W_2, every A[M]-linear map U ⊗ W_1 → U ⊗ W_2 is strict (A = End_M(U)).
hypotheses: The condition concerns only the Lie algebra; it is automatic for smooth U and V.
proofSteps: The canonical lifting J_P(V) → V^{N_0} ⊆ V and the U(g)-action on V give the (g, P)-map; its kernel is compared with that of U(g) ⊗ U → Ind U.
Maps coming from I(U) → V are balanced because they factor through the image of U(g) ⊗ U in Ind U (EMJ2 (0.7)).
acceptance: For U and V smooth every map is balanced, recovering the smooth Frobenius reciprocity (0.2) of EMJ2.

nodes.title: Emerton's adjunction theorem
nodes.statement: If U ∈ Rep^{zla.c}(M) is allowable and V is a very strongly admissible locally analytic representation of G, then the map Hom_G(I_{P^-}^G(U), V) → L_M(U(δ_P), J_P(V))^bal induced by J_P is an isomorphism. In particular, for a locally analytic character δ of T and P = B: Hom_G(I_{B^-}^G(δ), V) ≅ Hom_T(δδ_B, J_B(V))^bal.
hypotheses: U allowable; V very strongly admissible (the Banach embedding controls growth).
proofSteps: Injectivity: I(U) is generated by the image of U, which is determined by its Jacquet-module image.

Surjectivity: a balanced map defines a (g, P)-map on U(g) ⊗ C^sm_c(N, U) factoring through the coimage I(U)^lp(N); EMJ2 Corollary 4.3.3 extends it continuously to I(U)(N) using very strong admissibility, and G-equivariance spreads it to I(U).
acceptance: For U = δ a smooth character and V smooth admissible, the theorem is the smooth Frobenius reciprocity Hom_G((Ind δ)^∞, V) ≅ Hom_T(δδ_B, V_N).

sources.locator: Introduction, Theorem 0.13, p. 4; sketch of proof, p. 4
sources.match: For allowable U and very strongly admissible V the map (0.10) from G-maps out of I_P^G(U) to balanced maps into J_P(V) is an isomorphism; the proof passes through the (g, P)-invariant subspace of functions supported on the big cell.
For very strongly admissible V, an isomorphism L_G(X, V) → L_(g,P)(X^lp(N), V) on which the proof of Theorem 0.13 rests.
Uses Emerton's Definition 0.8 and Theorem 0.13 to pass between T-eigenvectors in J_B and G-maps from I_{B^-}^G.

nodes.title: Breuil's adjunction for Orlik–Strauch representations
nodes.statement: Let Q=MN be the Jacquet parabolic, Q⁻ its opposite (the inducing parabolic), W a finite-dimensional algebraic M-representation inflated to Q⁻, and π a smooth admissible finite-length M-representation. For very strongly admissible Π there is a natural isomorphism Hom_G(F^G_{Q⁻}((U(g_E)⊗_{U(q⁻_E)}W)^∨, π δ_Q^{-1}),Π) ≅ Hom_M(W′⊗π,J_Q(Π)). Equivalently the right side is Hom_{M^+}(W′⊗π,Π^{N_0}) for the averaged Hecke action. Breuil writes the same result with unaveraged Hecke operators and untwisted smooth inducing π; multiplying that action by δ_Q converts to this formula. The σ-analytic variant holds. For products, BHS Lemma 5.2.1 gives Hom_G(F^G_{B⁻}(Hom_E(M_0,E)^{u∞}, V δ_B^{-1}),Π) ≅ Hom_{T^+}(V,Hom_{U(g)}(M_0,Π)^{U_0}) for category-O M_0 and smooth finite-length admissible T-representation V, with the averaged Hecke action.
hypotheses: 𝐆 split connected reductive over L, B = TN ⊆ P = L_P N_P a Borel and a parabolic (standard or opposite), E/ℚ_p finite splitting L; O^p_alg is the category of the gap 'Category O and Kostant homology' for the ℚ_p-Lie algebra g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E = ∏_σ g_σ: finitely generated U(g ⊗ E)-modules, direct sums of simple algebraic U(l_P ⊗ E)-modules, locally finite for n_P ⊗ E.
Π very strongly admissible; π_P of finite length.

Use the ℚ_p-analytic residue-characteristic assumptions of LR.5. The restricted BHS smooth input ensures the Orlik–Strauch functor stays in its declared admissible domain; the source’s broader smooth statement may be treated after extending that domain.

The superscript ∨ on the category-O module denotes the restricted BGG dual defined by a root-reversing anti-involution that fixes the Cartan, as in BR15 pp. 14–15; it preserves highest weights and simple modules. It is distinct from the ordinary contragredient W′, which negates torus weights.
proofSteps: Apply BR15 Proposition 4.2: identify the compactly supported locally polynomial vectors of the differential-equation kernel with the appropriate restricted category-O dual tensored with C_c^∞(N,π). It is polynomially generated in bounded degree. EMJ2 Corollary 4.3.3 extends the resulting (g,Q)-map into Π continuously; this is not a blanket identification with I(U).

The compact-support/Jacquet adjunction (EMJ1 Theorem 3.5.6) gives the positive-monoid Hom. BR15 §4, (18), p. 13, uses the unaveraged sum, so replace its π by π δ_Q^{-1} to obtain the averaged-Jacquet formula. BHS (5.9), p. 391, writes δ_B times the sum and its Lemma 5.2.1 already includes exactly this inverse-modulus twist.

For products, use the compact-base tensor description from LR.5/orlik-strauch-products and run this polynomial-generation and growth argument on the factors; BHS Remark 5.1.2, p. 388, records the extension. No LR.6 result is used earlier in LR.5.
acceptance: For Q=B, W has weight −s_{i,σ}·λ, π=w(φ)ηδ_B, and Π=C(I,s_{i,σ}). The formula gives Hom_T(z^{s_{i,σ}·λ}w(φ)ηδ_B,J_B(Π))≅E as in Ding Lemma 3.2, with the corrected positive inducing weight. The negative weight belongs to the category-O input, not to the inducing character.

sources.match: Breuil’s positive-monoid Hom uses the unaveraged Hecke sum, explicitly distinguished from Emerton’s action on p. 13. Translating to the averaged J_Q requires the inverse-modulus twist on the smooth Orlik–Strauch argument and the opposite inducing parabolic.

Remarque 4.4 rewrites the unaveraged convention using a Jacquet functor and gives the σ-analytic variant. In this packet the averaged convention is fixed throughout, with its explicit modulus conversion.

For M in category O and V a smooth representation of T_p, Hom_G(F^{G_p}_{B_p}(Hom(M, L)^{u∞}, V δ^{-1}), Π̂^an) ≃ Hom_{T_p^+}(V, Hom_{U(g)}(M, Π̂^an)^{U_0}), functorially in M, using Breuil's Proposition 4.2 and the very strong admissibility.

nodes.title: Weights, twists and parameter spaces for GL_n(L)
nodes.statement: Fix n ≥ 1, L, E, Σ_L and d_L as above; T ⊆ B ⊆ GL_n is the diagonal torus in the upper Borel, B^- the lower Borel, N and N^- their unipotent radicals. (i) θ := (0, −1, …, 1 − n); for a standard parabolic P ⊇ B with Levi L_P ≅ GL_{n_1} × ⋯ × GL_{n_r}, θ^P := (0^{n_1}, (−n_1)^{n_2}, …, (−(n_1 + ⋯ + n_{r−1}))^{n_r}), an algebraic character of L_P, with θ^B = θ; for 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1, P_i is the maximal parabolic whose Levi L_i ≅ GL_i × GL_{n−i} has simple roots {1, …, n−1} ∖ {i}. (ii) For a character φ = φ_1 ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ φ_n of T(L) and w ∈ S_n, w(φ) := φ_{w^{-1}(1)} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ φ_{w^{-1}(n)}; φ is generic if φ_iφ_j^{-1} ∉ {1, |·|_L} for i ≠ j, where |·|_L is the unramified character with |ϖ_L|_L = p^{−[L_0:ℚ_p]}. (iii) δ_B = |·|_L^{n−1} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ |·|_L^{n+1−2i} ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ |·|_L^{1−n}; η := 1 ⊠ |·|_L ⊠ ⋯ ⊠ |·|_L^{n−1} = |·|_L^{-1} ∘ θ; ε := N_{L/ℚ_p}(·)|·|_L (the cyclotomic character through local class field theory sending a uniformiser to a geometric Frobenius). (iv) A weight h = (h_{σ,i}) ∈ ℤ^{Σ_L × {1,…,n}} is strictly dominant if h_{σ,1} > ⋯ > h_{σ,n} for every σ; then λ := h − θ^{[L:ℚ_p]}, λ_{σ,i} = h_{σ,i} + i − 1, is dominant; z^μ is the algebraic character diag(t_i) ↦ ∏_{σ,i} σ(t_i)^{μ_{σ,i}}; W_Σ := S_n^{Σ_L} acts on weights by the dot action u·μ := u(μ + ρ) − ρ, lg(u) := Σ_σ lg(u_σ), and s_{i,σ} is the simple reflection (i, i+1) in the σ-factor. (v) Hom(T(L), E), Hom_sm(T(L), E) and Hom_σ(T(L), E) are the locally ℚ_p-analytic, smooth and locally σ-analytic additive characters, and Hom_{g′}(T(L), E) := {ψ : ψ − ψ_0 ∘ det ∈ Hom_sm(T(L), E) for some ψ_0 ∈ Hom(L^×, E)}; Hom_{σ,g′} := Hom_{g′} ∩ Hom_σ.
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
Ding's K and E are this roadmap's L and E; Ding's d_K is d_L.
proofSteps: η = |·|_L^{-1} ∘ θ: the i-th entry of θ is 1 − i, so |·|_L^{−(1−i)} = |·|_L^{i−1}.
λ dominant: h_{σ,i} ≥ h_{σ,i+1} + 1 gives λ_{σ,i} = h_{σ,i} + i − 1 ≥ h_{σ,i+1} + i = λ_{σ,i+1}.
dim Hom_{g′}(T(L), E) = n + d_L by LR.4/torus-ext (4).
acceptance: η z^λ = z^h · (ε^{-1} ∘ θ) as characters of T(L) (the computation is in LR.7/principal-series-ps).

nodes.title: The locally algebraic representation π_alg(φ, h)
nodes.statement: For φ generic, I_sm(φ) := (Ind_{B^-(L)}^{GL_n(L)} φη)^∞ is an absolutely irreducible smooth admissible representation, I_sm(φ) ≅ I_sm(w(φ)) =: π_sm(φ) for all w ∈ S_n (the smooth representation attached to the Weil–Deligne representation ⊕φ_i by the classical local Langlands correspondence), and π_alg(φ, h) := π_sm(φ) ⊗_E L(λ) is an irreducible locally algebraic representation of GL_n(L), isomorphic to I_sm(w(φ)) ⊗_E L(λ) for every w. Fix isomorphisms π_alg(φ, h) ≅ L(λ) ⊗_E I_sm(w(φ)) for all w ((3.2) of Ding); the constructions of LR.7–LR.9 are independent of these choices up to the scalars that cancel in Ext¹ (Ding Remark 3.4). End_G(π_alg(φ, h)) = E.
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: Irreducibility and independence of the order of the generic smooth principal series: SR.3/generic-irreducibility (Bernstein–Zelevinsky).

π_alg(φ, h) is admissible and topologically irreducible by LR.1/locally-algebraic-representation (ST01 Proposition 3.4); End = E by Schur's lemma for absolutely irreducible admissible representations.

nodes.title: The locally analytic principal series PS(w(φ), h) and its constituents C(w, u)
nodes.statement: For w ∈ S_n put PS(w(φ), h) := (Ind_{B^-(L)}^{GL_n(L)} w(φ)ηz^λ)^{ℚ_p-an} = (Ind_{B^-(L)}^{GL_n(L)} w(φ)z^h(ε^{-1} ∘ θ))^{ℚ_p-an} (LR.4/principal-series). For u ∈ W_Σ = S_n^{Σ_L} put C(w, u) := F^{GL_n}_{B^-}(L^-(−u·λ), w(φ)η), where M^-(μ) := U(gl_{n,Σ_L}) ⊗_{U(b^-_{Σ_L})} μ is the Verma module for b^- and L^-(μ) its simple quotient (for μ antidominant, L^-(μ) is finite-dimensional, isomorphic to L(−μ)^∨). Then PS(w(φ), h) = F^{GL_n}_{B^-}(M^-(−λ), w(φ)η), and π_alg(φ, h) = C(w, 1) ⊆ PS(w(φ), h) through the fixed isomorphisms.
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: The two expressions agree: on t = diag(t_1, …, t_n), z^θ(t) = ∏_i N_{L/ℚ_p}(t_i)^{1−i} and (ε^{-1} ∘ θ)(t) = ∏_i ε(t_i)^{i−1} = ∏_i (N_{L/ℚ_p}(t_i)|t_i|_L)^{i−1}, so z^θ·(ε^{-1} ∘ θ) = ∏_i |t_i|_L^{i−1} = η and z^h(ε^{-1} ∘ θ) = z^λ z^θ (ε^{-1} ∘ θ) = z^λ η.

PS = F(M^-(−λ), w(φ)η) is LR.5/orlik-strauch-functor for a Verma module (ker φ = 0), with W the weight −λ, W′ = z^λ; C(w, 1) = F(L^-(−λ), w(φ)η) ≅ L(λ) ⊗ I_sm(w(φ)) by LR.5/orlik-strauch-transitivity with Q = G.

nodes.title: Constituents and socle of the locally analytic principal series (Ding, Proposition 3.1)
nodes.statement: For w ∈ S_n: (1) the irreducible constituents of PS(w(φ), h) are the C(w, u), u ∈ W_Σ, which are pairwise non-isomorphic, and those with lg(u) = 1 have multiplicity one; (2) soc_G PS(w(φ), h) ≅ I_sm(w(φ)) ⊗_E L(λ) ≅ π_alg(φ, h); (3) soc_G (PS(w(φ), h)/π_alg(φ, h)) ≅ ⊕_{u ∈ W_Σ, lg(u)=1} C(w, u); (4) for w, w′ ∈ S_n and u, u′ with lg(u) = lg(u′) = 1, C(w, u) ≅ C(w′, u′) if and only if u = u′ = s_{i,σ} for some i ∈ {1, …, n−1}, σ ∈ Σ_L, and w(w′)^{-1} lies in the Weyl group of L_{P_i}.
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.

The composition factors of M^-(−λ) are the L^-(−u·λ), u ∈ W_Σ, each with multiplicity given by Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, and multiplicity one for lg(u) ≤ 1; the socle/cosocle structure of the Verma module: inputs of the gap 'Category O and Kostant homology' (Humphreys Chapters 4–6, 8).
proofSteps: (1): by LR.5/orlik-strauch-jordan-holder the constituents of F(M^-(−λ), w(φ)η) are F^G_{Q_u}(L^-(−u·λ), i(w(φ)η)) over composition factors of the Verma module; for u ≠ 1 the maximal parabolic of L^-(−u·λ) is a proper one, and genericity makes the smooth induction to it irreducible, so C(w, u) is irreducible (LR.5/orlik-strauch-irreducibility); multiplicities are Verma multiplicities, one when lg(u) ≤ 1.

For (2), apply BR16 Corollary 2.5, pp. 11–12, to the simple quotient of the lower Verma and the generic smooth input. For (3), Ding Proposition 3.1(3), p. 34, verifies the claimed second socle layer, but the proposed proof by full faithfulness is not closed: OR19 Theorem 1 is locally L-analytic with trivial smooth argument. The ℚ_p-analytic result with this generic smooth argument needs the precise first-two-layer transport contract recorded in the gaps; it is not deduced from that narrower theorem.

(4): by LR.5/orlik-strauch-irreducibility (uniqueness), C(w, s_{i,σ}) = F^G_{P_i^-}(L^-(−s_{i,σ}·λ), i^{L_i}(w(φ)η)) is determined by the smooth induction to L_i, which is invariant exactly under the Weyl group of L_{P_i}.
acceptance: For n = 2, L = ℚ_p: PS(w(φ), h) is a nonsplit extension of C(w, s) by π_alg(φ, h), and C(1, s) ≇ C(s, s).

sources.match: States (1)–(4); (1) and (4) follow from Orlik–Strauch with the standard facts on constituents of Verma modules (Humphreys, Chapter 6), (2) and (3) from Orlik's Theorem 1.
Socle of F^G_P(M, π_P) and of the induction, and the uniqueness criterion for F^G_{Q_i}(M_i, π_{Q_i}).

nodes.title: The constituents C(I, s_{i,σ})
nodes.statement: For 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1, σ ∈ Σ_L and I ⊆ {1, …, n} with #I = i, all C(w, s_{i,σ}) with w^{-1}({1, …, i}) = I are isomorphic (LR.7/principal-series-constituents (4)); their common isomorphism class is C(I, s_{i,σ}). The C(I, s_{i,σ}) are pairwise distinct for distinct (I, i, σ), and C(I, s_{i,σ}) ≅ soc_G (Ind_{B^-(L)}^{GL_n(L)} z^{s_{i,σ}·λ} w(φ)η)^{ℚ_p-an} for any w with w^{-1}({1, …, i}) = I. The labels run over all nonempty proper subsets I ⊂ {1, …, n} (#I = i determines i), giving (2^n − 2)·d_L constituents in total.
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: The equality criterion in Proposition 3.1(4) is w(w′)^{-1}∈W_i, so w and w′ lie in the same left coset W_iw. This is equivalent to w^{-1}({1,…,i})=(w′)^{-1}({1,…,i}). It gives well-definedness and distinctness; the forward-image convention printed immediately after that proposition is inconsistent with its permutation action.
Socle realisation: by LR.5/orlik-strauch-jordan-holder (2) the socle of (Ind z^{s·λ}w(φ)η)^an is F^G_{P_i^-}(L^-(−s_{i,σ}·λ), soc i^{L_i}(w(φ)η)), which is C(w, s_{i,σ}).
Count: Σ_{i=1}^{n−1} binom(n, i) = 2^n − 2 subsets, times d_L embeddings.
acceptance: For n = 2 the labels are I = {1}, {2} with i = 1, giving C({1}, s_{1,σ}) and C({2}, s_{1,σ}) for each σ: 2d_L constituents.

nodes.statement: Let w ∈ S_n with w^{-1}({1, …, i}) = I. (1) Hom_{T(L)}(z^{s_{i,σ}·λ}w(φ)ηδ_B, J_B(C(I, s_{i,σ}))) ≅ E. (2) I_{B^-(L)}^{GL_n(L)}(z^{s_{i,σ}·λ}w(φ)η) ≅ C(I, s_{i,σ}). (Ding prints T(ℚ_p) for T(L) in (1); see sourceIssues.)
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: Every constituent of PS(w(φ), h) embeds into some locally analytic principal series (LR.5/orlik-strauch-jordan-holder (2)), so it is very strongly admissible (LR.4/locally-analytic-induction with LR.2/very-strongly-admissible).
(1): LR.6/orlik-strauch-jacquet-adjunction with P = B computes Hom_T(z^{s·λ}w(φ)ηδ_B, J_B(C)) as Hom_G(C(I, s), C) = E.

(2): the T-eigenline of (1) lies in J_B(C(I, s)) ⊆ J_B((Ind z^{s·λ}w(φ)η)^an) because Hom_T into J_B of every other constituent vanishes; by the definition of I_{B^-}^G (LR.6/closed-induction) its G-span is the socle C(I, s).

nodes.title: The representations PS_1(w(φ), h) and π_1(φ, h)
nodes.statement: PS_1(w(φ), h) ⊆ PS(w(φ), h) is the unique subrepresentation with socle π_alg(φ, h) and cosocle ⊕_{1≤i≤n−1, σ∈Σ_L} C(w, s_{i,σ}). Using the fixed isomorphisms π_alg(φ, h) ≅ L(λ) ⊗ I_sm(w(φ)) ↪ PS_1(w(φ), h), the amalgamated sum ⊕^{w∈S_n}_{π_alg(φ,h)} PS_1(w(φ), h) has a unique quotient π_1(φ, h) with socle π_alg(φ, h). π_1(φ, h) is an extension of ⊕_{i, σ, #I=i} C(I, s_{i,σ}) ((2^n − 2)d_L constituents, each once) by π_alg(φ, h), with tautological injections π_alg(φ, h) ↪ π_1(φ, h) and PS_1(w(φ), h) ↪ π_1(φ, h); it depends only on (φ, h). End_G(π_1(φ, h)) = E, and restriction to the socle gives End(π_1) ≅ End(π_alg) = E.
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness of PS_1: by LR.7/principal-series-constituents (2)–(3), the preimage in PS of soc(PS/π_alg) is the required subrepresentation.

Put A=π_alg. The finite amalgam M has A with composition multiplicity one, because each PS_1 has one A and the amalgamation identifies those copies. Every subrepresentation disjoint from A has no A composition factor; finite sums retain that property and remain disjoint from A. Finite length therefore gives a largest such R. The image of A is essential in M/R, so its socle is A; conversely a quotient retaining A with that socle must kill exactly R. To identify repeated C(w,s)-extensions and obtain each C(I,s) once, use the rank-one constituent identifications and compatible embeddings in BH20 Proposition 5.9, pp. 27–28, together with the first-two-layer contract. This is not a consequence of an arbitrary lattice argument or of an unread Ext-dimension assertion.

End = E: an endomorphism minus the scalar by which it acts on the socle kills the socle, so its image is a subrepresentation isomorphic to a quotient of π_1/π_alg = ⊕ C(I, s); since soc(π_1) = π_alg contains no C(I, s), the image is 0.
acceptance: For n = 2, L = ℚ_p: π_1(φ, h) is the amalgam of PS_1(φ, h) = PS(φ, h) and PS_1(s(φ), h) = PS(s(φ), h) over π_alg, with cosocle C({1}, s) ⊕ C({2}, s).

V = π_1(φ, h), its first two socle layers, End(π) → End(V) → End(A) ≅ E

nodes.title: Self-extensions of π_alg(φ, h) (Ding, Proposition 3.3)
nodes.statement: (1) For w ∈ S_n and ψ ∈ Hom_{g′}(T(L), E), I_{B^-(L)}^{GL_n(L)}(w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε)) is an extension of π_alg(φ, h) by itself, and ζ_w : Hom_{g′}(T(L), E) → Ext^1_{GL_n(L)}(π_alg(φ, h), π_alg(φ, h)), ψ ↦ I_{B^-}(w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε)), is bijective and restricts to Hom_sm(T(L), E) ≅ Ext^1_lalg(π_alg, π_alg); hence dim Ext^1_lalg = n and dim Ext^1_{GL_n(L)}(π_alg, π_alg) = n + d_L. Explicitly, for ψ = ψ_1 + ψ_0 ∘ det with ψ_1 smooth, I(w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε)) ≅ (Ind_{B^-} w(φ)η(1 + ψ_1ε))^∞ ⊗ L(λ) ⊗_{E[ε]} (1 + εψ_0 ∘ det). (2) For w_1, w_2 ∈ S_n, ζ_{w_2} ∘ (w_2w_1^{-1}) = ζ_{w_1} on Hom_{g′}(T(L), E), where w_2w_1^{-1} acts by permuting coordinates. ζ_w does not depend on the isomorphisms (3.2).
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: The canonical embedding w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε)δ_B ↪ J_B((Ind …)^an) factors through (Ind w(φ)η(1 + ψ_1ε))^∞ ⊗ L(λ) ⊗ (1 + εψ_0 ∘ det); by the definition of I (LR.6/closed-induction) this is the closed induction, an E[ε]-self-extension of π_alg.

With central character fixed, Ext^1_{lalg,Z} ≅ Ext^1_{G,Z} (LR.1/locally-algebraic-ext), and smooth theory gives Hom_sm(T/Z, E) ≅ Ext^1_{lalg,Z} (dimension n − 1); comparing 0 → Hom_sm(T/Z) → Hom_{g′}(T) → Hom(Z(L), E) → 0 with 0 → Ext^1_Z → Ext^1 → Hom(Z(L), E) → 0 shows ζ_w bijective.

On smooth characters, SR.3/part-ii-ordered-character-map gives 𝒥_{w_2}∘p_{w_2w_1^{-1}}=𝒥_{w_1}, where p is the permutation of the parameter torus. Its differential gives ζ_{w_2}∘(w_2w_1^{-1})=ζ_{w_1}. Determinant twists are invariant under permutations, extending the identity to Hom_{g′}. The opposite composition printed in the original packet was not the source diagram.
acceptance: For n = 1: Ext^1_{L^×}(χ, χ) = Hom(L^×, E) of dimension 1 + d_L, Ext^1_lalg of dimension 1.

sources.locator: §3.1.2, Proposition 3.3, (3.4)–(3.6), its proof and Remark 3.4, pp. 35–36
sources.match: Constructs ζ_w through Emerton's closed induction of deformed characters, proves bijectivity using Schraen's Proposition 4.7 for the fixed-central-character part and a comparison of exact sequences with Hom(Z(K), E), and proves (2) through the tangent maps of the Bernstein-centre maps 𝒥_w of Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin Lemma 3.22.

nodes.title: One-dimensional extension groups with a constituent (Ding, Lemma 3.5)
nodes.statement: For every C(I, s_{i,σ}): (1) dim_E Ext^1_{GL_n(L)}(C(I, s_{i,σ}), π_alg(φ, h)) = dim_E Ext^1_{GL_n(L)}(π_alg(φ, h), C(I, s_{i,σ})) = 1; more precisely Ext^1(π_alg, C(I, s_{i,σ})) ≅ Ext^1(π_alg, (Ind_{B^-} z^{s_{i,σ}·λ}w(φ)η)^an) ≅ Hom_{T(L)}(H_1(N^-(L), π_alg), z^{s_{i,σ}·λ}w(φ)η) ≅ E. (2) For a nonsplit π̃_alg(φ, h) ∈ Ext^1(π_alg, π_alg), pull-back along π̃_alg ↠ π_alg is a bijection Ext^1(π_alg, C(I, s_{i,σ})) ≅ Ext^1(π̃_alg, C(I, s_{i,σ})).
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.

The equality dim Ext^1(C(I, s_{i,σ}), π_alg) = 1 (extensions in the other direction) is quoted by Ding from Breuil–Qian (arXiv 2024, Proposition 5.1.14 with Lemma 3.2.4(ii)); no target of this roadmap uses that direction, and it is recorded as an imported statement with the gap 'Breuil–Qian dimension'.
proofSteps: Schraen's spectral sequence for Σ = π_alg and ρ = δ := z^{s·λ}w(φ)η (separatedness: π_alg is locally algebraic) has E_2^{p,q} = Ext^p_T(H_q(N^-, π_alg), δ) (LR.4/schraen-spectral-sequence).

H_q(N^-, π_alg) = H_q(n^-, L(λ)) ⊗ J_{N^-}(I_sm(φ)) with J_{N^-}(I_sm(φ)) ≅ ⊕_{w′} w′(φ)η (SR.2/principal-series-jacquet) and Kostant (LR.4/unipotent-homology); Ext between distinct torus characters vanishes (LR.4/torus-ext), so in total degree 1 only Hom_T(H_1(N^-, π_alg), δ) ≅ Hom_T(δ, δ) = E survives.
Push-forward along C(I, s) ↪ (Ind δ)^an is an isomorphism on Ext^1(π_alg, −) because the other constituents have lg ≥ 2 relative to λ (LR.5/ext-vanishing-long-weyl).

(2): the same computation with π̃_alg (whose restriction to SL_n(L) is locally algebraic, so separatedness holds) gives Ext^1(π̃_alg, C(I, s)) ≅ Hom_T(w(φ)ηz^{s·λ}(1 + ψε), w(φ)ηz^{s·λ}) with ψ = ζ_w^{-1}(π̃_alg) ≠ 0, which is one-dimensional; the pull-back is injective by dévissage, hence bijective.
acceptance: For n = 2, L = ℚ_p: Ext^1(π_alg, C({1}, s)) and Ext^1(π_alg, C({2}, s)) are each one-dimensional.

sources.match: States (1)–(2); proves (2) and the second equality of (1) with Schraen's spectral sequence (the separatedness hypothesis holds for π_alg and its self-extensions), the vanishing of Ext between distinct torus characters, Schraen's (4.40)–(4.42), the classical Jacquet module of I_sm(φ) and Ding's Lemma 2.26; the first equality is quoted from Breuil–Qian Proposition 5.1.14 and Lemma 3.2.4(ii).

nodes.title: The maps ζ_w : Hom(T(L), E) → Ext^1(π_alg(φ, h), π_1(φ, h))
nodes.statement: For w ∈ S_n, sending ψ ∈ Hom(T(L), E) to (Ind_{B^-(L)}^{GL_n(L)} w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε))^{ℚ_p-an} ∈ Ext^1(PS(w(φ), h), PS(w(φ), h)), pulling back along π_alg(φ, h) ↪ PS(w(φ), h) and using the push-forward isomorphism Ext^1(π_alg, PS_1(w(φ), h)) ≅ Ext^1(π_alg, PS(w(φ), h)) (Ding 2019, Lemma 2.26: the constituents of PS/PS_1 have lg ≥ 2) gives the map (3.10) Hom(T(L), E) → Ext^1(π_alg, PS_1(w(φ), h)); composing with push-forward along PS_1(w(φ), h) ↪ π_1(φ, h) gives ζ_w : Hom(T(L), E) → Ext^1_{GL_n(L)}(π_alg(φ, h), π_1(φ, h)) ((3.11)). Equivalently, I_{B^-}(w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε)) ⊆ (Ind w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε))^an is an extension of π_alg by a subrepresentation V ⊆ PS_1(w(φ), h), and ζ_w(ψ) is its push-forward along V ↪ PS_1 ↪ π_1 (Remark 3.7). ζ_w does not depend on the isomorphisms (3.2).
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: (Ind w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε))^an is an E[ε]-self-extension of PS(w(φ), h) (LR.1/self-extension-dual-numbers, LR.4/locally-analytic-induction); pull back along π_alg ↪ PS.
The push-forward Ext^1(π_alg, PS_1) → Ext^1(π_alg, PS) is an isomorphism by LR.5/ext-vanishing-long-weyl and dévissage; invert it, then push forward to π_1.
Remark 3.7: the closed induction I(w(φ)ηz^λ(1 + ψε)) (LR.6/closed-induction) lies in the deformed induction and maps onto π_alg with kernel inside PS_1, giving the same class.
acceptance: On Hom_{g′}(T(L), E), ζ_w is the composite of the bijection of LR.7/self-extensions with push-forward along π_alg ↪ π_1 (Ding, Proposition 3.6(2)).

nodes.title: Ext^1(π_alg, PS_1) is Hom(T(L), E) (Ding, Proposition 3.6)
nodes.statement: (1) For w ∈ S_n the map (3.10) Hom(T(L), E) → Ext^1_{GL_n(L)}(π_alg(φ, h), PS_1(w(φ), h)) is bijective; in particular dim_E Ext^1(π_alg, PS_1(w(φ), h)) = n + n·d_L = dim Hom(T(L), E). Equivalently ζ_w : Hom(T(L), E) ≅ Ext^1(π_alg, PS(w(φ), h)). (2) ζ_w restricted to Hom_{g′}(T(L), E) equals (3.4) followed by the push-forward Ext^1(π_alg, π_alg) ↪ Ext^1(π_alg, π_1(φ, h)).
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: Schraen's spectral sequence for Σ = π_alg, ρ = w(φ)ηz^λ: E_2^{0,1} = Hom_T(H_1(N^-, π_alg), ρ) = 0 (the weights of H_1 are s·λ-type, different from λ), and E_2^{1,0} = Ext^1_T(H_0(N^-, π_alg), ρ) = Ext^1_T(ρ, ρ) ≅ Hom(T(L), E) (LR.4/torus-ext), the other characters of H_0 contributing nothing.
Hence Ext^1(π_alg, PS(w(φ), h)) ≅ Hom(T(L), E), and the push-forward from PS_1 is an isomorphism (LR.5/ext-vanishing-long-weyl); the resulting map agrees with (3.10) by construction.
(2): both maps send ψ ∈ Hom_{g′} to the class of the locally algebraic-twisted closed induction (LR.7/self-extensions, LR.7/zeta-w).

nodes.title: The extension group Ext^1(π_alg(φ, h), π_1(φ, h)) (Ding, Proposition 3.8)
nodes.statement: (1) There is an exact sequence 0 → Ext^1(π_alg, π_alg) → Ext^1(π_alg, π_1(φ, h)) → ⊕_{1≤i≤n−1, σ∈Σ_L, I⊆{1,…,n}, #I=i} Ext^1(π_alg, C(I, s_{i,σ})) → 0 (the source prints I ⊆ {1, …, n−1}; see sourceIssues), so dim_E Ext^1_{GL_n(L)}(π_alg(φ, h), π_1(φ, h)) = n + (2^n − 1)d_L. (2) The map t_{φ,h} := (ζ_w)_w : ⊕_{w∈S_n} Hom(T(L), E) → Ext^1(π_alg, π_1(φ, h)) is surjective. (3) (Remark 3.9.) The push-forward Ext^1(π_alg, π_1(φ, h)) → Ext^1(π_alg, π(φ, h)) is an isomorphism (LR.7/finite-slope-amalgam), so (2) holds with π(φ, h) in place of π_1(φ, h).
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: Dévissage of 0 → π_alg → π_1 → ⊕ C(I, s) → 0 with Hom(π_alg, C(I, s)) = 0 gives the left part of the sequence; it suffices to show the last map surjective.

For each w, 0 → Ext^1(π_alg, π_alg) → Ext^1(π_alg, PS_1(w(φ), h)) → ⊕_{i,σ} Ext^1(π_alg, C(w, s_{i,σ})) is exact (3.14), and by dimensions (n + d_L, n + nd_L and (n−1)d_L one-dimensional terms; LR.7/self-extensions, LR.7/ext-ps1, LR.7/constituent-ext-lines) the last map is surjective.
Every C(I, s_{i,σ}) is a C(w, s_{i,σ}) for some w, so varying w covers the target (3.15); this gives (1) and, with LR.7/ext-ps1, the surjectivity (2). The dimension is (n + d_L) + (2^n − 2)d_L.
acceptance: For n = 2, L = ℚ_p: dim Ext^1(π_alg, π_1) = 2 + 3 = 5, while ⊕_{w} Hom(T, E) has dimension 8.

nodes.title: The amalgam π(φ, h) of the principal series
nodes.statement: π(φ, h) is the unique quotient of the amalgamated sum ⊕^{w∈S_n}_{π_alg(φ,h)} PS(w(φ), h) (over the fixed π_alg ↪ PS(w(φ), h)) with socle π_alg(φ, h); it is the representation π(ρ)^{fs} of Breuil–Herzig (Definition 5.7) in this setting. π_1(φ, h) is the subrepresentation formed by the first two layers of the socle filtration of π(φ, h), and push-forward along π_1(φ, h) ↪ π(φ, h) is an isomorphism Ext^1(π_alg, π_1(φ, h)) ≅ Ext^1(π_alg, π(φ, h)).
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: Each principal series has A=π_alg with composition multiplicity one (the length-zero Verma constituent), so the finite amalgam M also does. A subrepresentation disjoint from A has no A composition factor, and finite sums of these subrepresentations remain disjoint. Finite length gives their largest sum R. Then A embeds essentially into M/R and soc(M/R)=A. Any quotient of M preserving this socle kills precisely R; this proves uniqueness. Admissibility is preserved by the finite sums and quotients.
Its socle filtration: the first layer is π_alg, the second ⊕ C(I, s) (LR.7/principal-series-constituents (3)), so the first two layers form π_1.
Push-forward isomorphism: the constituents of π(φ, h)/π_1(φ, h) are C(w, u) with lg(u) ≥ 2, for which Ext^1(π_alg, −) and Hom(π_alg, −) vanish (LR.5/ext-vanishing-long-weyl).
acceptance: For n = 2 (and d_L = 1), π(φ, h) = π_1(φ, h) since PS has length 2.

nodes.title: Levi data of a P-filtration and the parabolic induction (3.19)
nodes.statement: Let P ⊇ B be a standard parabolic with Levi L_P = diag(GL_{n_1}, …, GL_{n_r}) and Weyl group W_P. A P-filtration F_P of ⊕_{i=1}^n φ_i is an ordering of the φ_i into consecutive blocks of sizes n_1, …, n_r; put φ_{F_P,i} := ⊗_{φ_j ∈ gr^i F_P} φ_j, h^i := (h_{n_1+⋯+n_{i−1}+1}, …, h_{n_1+⋯+n_i}) and λ^i the corresponding dominant weight. LR.7 applied to (φ_{F_P,i}, h^i) gives π_alg(φ_{F_P,i}, h^i) ⊆ π_1(φ_{F_P,i}, h^i) for GL_{n_i}(L); for n_i=1, put k=n_1+⋯+n_{i−1}+1 and let ψ_k be the unique smooth character in gr^i F_P; both representations equal ψ_k z^{h_k}. For an arbitrary filtration ψ_k need not be the original φ_k. The source’s missing +1 is also corrected (E4). Fixing compatible isomorphisms (transitivity of parabolic induction, matching (3.2) for all w ∈ W_Pw_0 refining F_P, with w_0 any one such ordering), there is an injection π_alg(φ, h) ≅ (Ind_{P^-(L)}^{GL_n(L)} (⊠_i π_alg(φ_{F_P,i}, h^i)) ε^{-1} ∘ θ^P)^{lalg} ↪ (Ind_{P^-(L)}^{GL_n(L)} (⊗̂_i π_1(φ_{F_P,i}, h^i)) ε^{-1} ∘ θ^P)^{ℚ_p-an} ((3.19)), with ⊗̂ the completed tensor product of LR.0/completed-external-tensor.
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: Transitivity of parabolic induction (LR.4/locally-analytic-induction) identifies I_sm(w(φ)) ⊗ L(λ) with the induction from P^- of ⊠_i I_sm(w_i(φ_{F_P,i})) ⊗ L(λ^i) twisted by ε^{-1} ∘ θ^P; the twist corrects the shift between λ and (λ^i)_i.

Choose a refinement T_{w_0} of F_P, whose ordered tuple is ψ_k=φ_{w_0^{-1}(k)}. All refinements form the left coset W_Pw_0. Choose the block isomorphisms first and transport by transitivity to that coset; it is W_P itself only for the standard filtration.
π_alg(φ_{F_P,i}, h^i) ↪ π_1(φ_{F_P,i}, h^i) and exactness of induction give (3.19).
acceptance: For P = B, every n_i = 1 and the injection is π_alg(φ, h) ↪ PS(w(φ), h) for the w attached to F_P.

nodes.title: Which constituents C(I, s_{i,σ}) occur in a parabolic induction (Ding, Lemma 3.10)
nodes.statement: For 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1, σ ∈ Σ_L and I ⊆ {1, …, n} with #I = i, C(I, s_{i,σ}) is an irreducible constituent of (Ind_{P^-}^{GL_n} (⊗̂_j π_1(φ_{F_P,j}, h^j)) ε^{-1} ∘ θ^P)^{ℚ_p-an} if and only if either (1) there is k with n_1 + ⋯ + n_{k−1} + 1 ≤ i ≤ n_1 + ⋯ + n_k − 1 and {j : φ_j ∈ Fil_{F_P}^{k−1}} ⊆ I ⊆ {j : φ_j ∈ Fil_{F_P}^k}, or (2) i = n_1 + ⋯ + n_k for some k ≤ r − 1 and I = {j : φ_j ∈ Fil_{F_P}^k}. Each such constituent has multiplicity one and lies in the socle of the quotient of the induction by π_alg(φ, h).
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
Multiplicity one of L^-(−s_{i,σ}·λ) in the parabolic Verma module and its position in the cosocle of the kernel to L^-(−λ) are inputs of the gap 'Category O and Kostant homology'.
proofSteps: Case (2) (i at a block boundary): the constituents come from V_0 = induction of ⊠_i π_alg(φ_{F_P,i}, h^i); they are F of the constituents L^-(−s_{i,σ}·λ) of the parabolic Verma module, multiplicity one and in the cosocle of the kernel, hence in the socle of the quotient by π_alg (LR.5/orlik-strauch-jordan-holder).

Case (1) (i inside a block): V_I := induction of ⊠_{i≠k} π_alg ⊠ C(I, s_{i,σ})_k embeds into (Ind z^{s·λ}w(φ)η)^an for w^{-1}({1, …, i}) = I, whose socle is C(I, s) with multiplicity one; a closed subrepresentation W of the principal series shows C(I, s) lies in the socle of the quotient by π_alg.
Every C(I, s) in the induction comes from V_0 or a V_I by exactness and Orlik–Strauch, with multiplicity one.
acceptance: For P = B: the condition reduces to I = w^{-1}({1, …, i}) for the w attached to F_P, i.e. the C(w, s_{i,σ}) of PS_1(w(φ), h).

nodes.statement: Let S_{F_P} be the set of constituents C(I, s_{i,σ}) satisfying LR.8/parabolic-constituents; #S_{F_P} = (Σ_{i=1}^r (2^{n_i} − 2) + (r − 1))·d_L ((3.21)). π_{F_P}(φ, h) is the unique subrepresentation of the parabolic induction (3.19) with socle π_alg(φ, h) and π_{F_P}(φ, h)/π_alg(φ, h) ≅ ⊕_{C∈S_{F_P}} C. For P = B and F_P = T_w, π_{F_P}(φ, h) ≅ PS_1(w(φ), h). The injection π_alg ↪ π_{F_P} extends uniquely to π_{F_P}(φ, h) ↪ π_1(φ, h); Ext^1_{F_P}(π_alg, π_1) denotes the image of the (injective) push-forward Ext^1(π_alg, π_{F_P}) → Ext^1(π_alg, π_1), and Ext^1_{F_P,g′} := ζ_{F_P}(∏_i Ext^1_{g′}(π_alg(φ_{F_P,i}, h^i), π_1(φ_{F_P,i}, h^i))) (LR.8/zeta-fp).
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: Existence and uniqueness: LR.8/parabolic-constituents puts every C ∈ S_{F_P} in the socle of the quotient by π_alg with multiplicity one; take the preimage.

Count: within block k, i ranges over n_{<k} + 1, …, n_{≤k} − 1 and I over the subsets between consecutive filtration steps, giving Σ_k (2^{n_k} − 2); at the r − 1 block boundaries there is one I each; times d_L.

nodes.title: The parabolic induction map ζ_{F_P}
nodes.statement: Write A_i=π_alg(φ_{F_P,i},h^i), B_i=π_1(φ_{F_P,i},h^i). Locally analytic induction twisted by ε^{-1}∘θ^P and pullback along (3.19) give Ext¹_{L_P}(⊠_i A_i,⊗̂_i B_i)→Ext¹_G(π_alg,(Ind …)^an)≅Ext¹_G(π_alg,π_{F_P}), as in (3.25). For extensions 0→B_i→X_i→A_i→0, filter ⊗̂_i X_i by the number of B-factors. Quotienting by filtration degree at least two gives 0→⊕_i(B_i⊠⊗̂_{j≠i}A_j)→V→⊠_i A_i→0. Map this kernel to ⊗̂_i B_i using each A_j↪B_j and addition, and push out. This gives (3.26) with its tensor factors corrected, and then ζ_{F_P}:∏_i Ext¹(A_i,B_i)→Ext¹_{F_P}(π_alg,π_1) by (3.27).
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: Strict exactness of completed compact-type external tensor products gives the tensor filtration and its first graded piece ⊕_i B_i⊠⊗̂_{j≠i}A_j. The quotient and pushout stay in the admissible category by LR.1/admissible-external-tensor and LR.1/admissible-abelian-category. This construction is additive and E-linear in the tuple of extension classes, not a multilinear product of them. Exact induction and pullback give (3.25).
The push-forward Ext^1(π_alg, π_{F_P}) → Ext^1(π_alg, Ind …) is bijective because the constituents of Ind/π_{F_P} have lg ≥ 2 (LR.5/ext-vanishing-long-weyl).
acceptance: For P = B, ζ_{F_P} on ∏_i Hom(L^×, E) = Hom(T(L), E) is ζ_w (LR.8/zeta-fp-bijective (2)).

nodes.title: The two endpoint parabolics amalgamate to π_1(φ, h) (Ding, Proposition 3.13)
nodes.statement: Let F be the filtration ⊕_{i≤n−1} φ_i ⊂ ⊕_i φ_i (parabolic P_{n−1}, Levi GL_{n−1} × GL_1) and G the filtration φ_n ⊂ ⊕_i φ_i (parabolic P_1, Levi GL_1 × GL_{n−1}). Then C(I, s_{i,σ}) occurs in π_F(φ, h) iff I ⊆ {1, …, n−1}, and in π_G(φ, h) iff I = I_1 ∪ {n} with I_1 ⊆ {1, …, n−1}; hence π_1/π_alg ≅ (π_F/π_alg) ⊕ (π_G/π_alg), and there are natural exact sequences 0 → π_alg(φ, h) → π_F(φ, h) ⊕ π_G(φ, h) → π_1(φ, h) → 0 and 0 → Ext^1_{g′}(π_alg, π_1) → Ext^1_F(π_alg, π_1) ⊕ Ext^1_G(π_alg, π_1) → Ext^1(π_alg, π_1) → 0, the first map b ↦ (b, −b). By LR.8/zeta-fp-bijective, ζ_F : Ext^1_{GL_{n−1}}(π_alg(φ^1, h^1), π_1(φ^1, h^1)) × Hom(L^×, E) ≅ Ext^1_F and similarly ζ_G. (The source prints P_1 and P_2 for the two parabolics; they are P_{n−1} and P_1 — see sourceIssues.)

n≥2, so the endpoint parabolics and their blocks of sizes n−1 and 1 exist.
proofSteps: Lemma 3.10 (LR.8/parabolic-constituents) for F and G gives the two constituent sets, which partition the (2^n − 2)d_L labels: a nonempty proper I either avoids n or contains it.
The first sequence follows since π_F and π_G meet exactly in π_alg inside π_1; applying Ext^1(π_alg, −) and Hom(π_alg, π_1) = E gives the second sequence up to right exactness.
Right exactness: dim Ext^1_F + dim Ext^1_G − dim Ext^1_{g′} = n + (2^n − 1)d_L by LR.8/ext-pi-fp, LR.7/self-extensions and LR.7/ext-pi1.

nodes.title: Locally σ-analytic and g_{Σ_L∖{σ}}-algebraic representations
nodes.statement: Let σ ∈ Σ_L. A locally ℚ_p-analytic representation V of a locally L-analytic group G over E is locally σ-analytic if the derived action of g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E = ∏_τ g_τ (LR.0/derived-lie-action) factors through g_σ = g ⊗_{L,σ} E, and g_{Σ_L∖{σ}}-algebraic if, for every v ∈ V, U(g_{Σ_L∖{σ}})·v is a finite-dimensional algebraic representation of g_{Σ_L∖{σ}} := ∏_{τ≠σ} g_τ. D_σ(G, E) is the quotient of D(G, E) acting on locally σ-analytic representations (the dual of the locally σ-analytic functions). For g_{Σ_L∖{σ}}-algebraic V, W, Ext^1_σ(V, W) ⊆ Ext^1_G(V, W) is the subspace of g_{Σ_L∖{σ}}-algebraic extensions; for admissible locally σ-analytic V, W it is Ext^1_{D_σ(G,E)}(W′, V′) (Breuil). For characters, Hom_σ(T(L), E) is the space of locally σ-analytic additive characters, and Hom_{σ,g′} := Hom_{g′} ∩ Hom_σ. (Ind_P^G U)^{σ-an} is the locally σ-analytic induction (LR.4/locally-analytic-induction).
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: The derived action decomposes along g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E ≅ ∏_τ g_τ (LR.0/rational-points-analytic-group); both conditions are conditions on that action.
Ext^1_σ is a subspace: g_{Σ∖σ}-algebraic extensions are closed under Baer sum and scalar multiplication.
acceptance: For L = ℚ_p (Σ_L = {σ}), every locally ℚ_p-analytic representation is locally σ-analytic and g_∅-algebraic, and Ext^1_σ = Ext^1.

nodes.title: The g_{Σ_L∖{σ}}-algebraic parts π_{1,σ}(φ, h) and PS_{1,σ}(w(φ), h)
nodes.statement: For σ ∈ Σ_L, π_{1,σ}(φ, h) ⊆ π_1(φ, h) is the subrepresentation which is an extension of ⊕_{1≤i≤n−1, #I=i} C(I, s_{i,σ}) (fixed σ, all I) by π_alg(φ, h); PS_{1,σ}(w(φ), h) ⊆ PS_1(w(φ), h) is the subrepresentation with constituents π_alg(φ, h) and C(w, s_{i,σ}), 1 ≤ i ≤ n−1, and PS_{1,σ}(w(φ), h) = PS_1(w(φ), h) ∩ ((Ind_{B^-} w(φ)ηz^{λ_σ})^{σ-an} ⊗_E L(λ^σ)) with λ_σ the σ-component of λ and λ^σ := (λ_τ)_{τ≠σ}. Moreover C(I, s_{i,σ}) ≅ F^{GL_n}_{B^-}(L^-(−s_{i,σ}·λ_σ), w(φ)η) ⊗_E L(λ^σ), with F^{GL_n}_{B^-}(L^-(−s_{i,σ}·λ_σ), w(φ)η) ↪ (Ind_{B^-} w(φ)ηz^{s_{i,σ}·λ_σ})^{σ-an} (the source drops the minus sign; see sourceIssues). π_{1,σ}(φ, h) is the unique quotient of ⊕^{w}_{π_alg(φ,h)} PS_{1,σ}(w(φ), h) with socle π_alg(φ, h), it is g_{Σ_L∖{σ}}-algebraic, and it is the maximal g_{Σ_L∖{σ}}-algebraic subrepresentation of π_1(φ, h). For a P-filtration, π_{F_P,σ}(φ, h) := π_{F_P}(φ, h) ∩ π_{1,σ}(φ, h), the maximal g_{Σ∖σ}-algebraic subrepresentation of π_{F_P}.
hypotheses: Setting of LR.7: L/ℚ_p finite (Ding's K), d_L = [L:ℚ_p], E/ℚ_p finite containing all embeddings Σ_L = {σ : L → E}; G = GL_n(L) with upper Borel B = TN, lower Borel B^- = TN^-, all inductions locally ℚ_p-analytic and unnormalised; φ a generic smooth character of T(L), h strictly dominant, λ = h − θ.
proofSteps: L^-(−s_{i,σ}·λ) = L^-_σ(−s_{i,σ}·λ_σ) ⊠ (⊠_{τ≠σ} L^-_τ(−λ_τ)) with finite-dimensional factors for τ ≠ σ, which gives the tensor decomposition of C(I, s_{i,σ}) and its g_{Σ∖σ}-algebraicity.

The constituents C(I, s_{i,τ}) with τ ≠ σ are not g_{Σ∖σ}-algebraic (their τ-component is infinite-dimensional), so the maximal g_{Σ∖σ}-algebraic subrepresentation of π_1 is π_{1,σ}; similarly for PS_{1,σ} inside the σ-analytic induction.
acceptance: For L = ℚ_p, π_{1,σ}(φ, h) = π_1(φ, h) and PS_{1,σ} = PS_1.

nodes.title: The σ-part of Ext^1(π_alg, π_1) and the decomposition over embeddings (Ding, Proposition 3.18)
nodes.statement: Let Ext^1_σ(π_alg, π_1) (respectively Ext^1_{σ,g′}) be the image of Ext^1_σ(π_alg, π_{1,σ}) (respectively Ext^1_σ(π_alg, π_alg)) under the injective push-forward; then Ext^1_{σ,g′} = Ext^1_{g′} ∩ Ext^1_σ. (1) 0 → Ext^1_σ(π_alg, π_alg) → Ext^1_σ(π_alg, π_1(φ, h)) → ⊕_{1≤i≤n−1, I⊆{1,…,n}, #I=i} Ext^1(π_alg, C(I, s_{i,σ})) → 0 is exact (the source prints I ⊆ {1, …, n−1}), and dim_E Ext^1_σ(π_alg, π_1) = n + 2^n − 1. gaps.title: Category O, Verma layers and dualised Kostant formulas (owner LieHighestWeightPartIICompletedCategoryO, not designed)
gaps.detail: The Orlik–Strauch layers and Ding's computations need, for g ⊗_{ℚ_p} E = ∏_σ g_σ with g split reductive: (a) the categories O and O^p_alg (finitely generated U(g ⊗ E)-modules, semisimple algebraic over l_P ⊗ E, locally finite over n_P ⊗ E; Orlik–Strauch §2.5, Breuil socle I §2 (i)–(iii)), abelian and artinian, closed under subobjects and quotients, O^q_alg ⊆ O^p_alg for q ⊇ p; (b) generalised Verma modules U(g) ⊗_{U(p)} W, their unique simple quotients, the maximal parabolic of a simple object and the classification of simple objects by highest weight (Humphreys §§9.3–9.4, Theorem 1.3); (c) for gl_n: the composition factors of the Verma module M^-(−λ), λ dominant, are the L^-(−u·λ), u ∈ W, with multiplicity one when lg(u) ≤ 1, the second radical layer is ⊕_{lg(u)=1} L^-(−u·λ), and multiplicity one of L^-(−s_{i,σ}·λ) in the parabolic Verma modules U(g) ⊗_{U(p)} (−λ) used in Ding's Lemma 3.10 (Humphreys Chapters 4–6, 8–9); (d) Kostant cohomology with the chosen positive roots, and homology obtained by H_q(n_P,W)=H^q(n_P,W∨)∨. The radical, dual and root twists must be fixed explicitly; the unadjusted cohomological w·λ formula is not a homology formula (Schraen Théorème 4.10, pp. 82–83). Upstream LieHighestWeight excludes full category O; the accepted LieHighestWeightPartII packet proposes the split-off roadmap LieHighestWeightPartIICompletedCategoryO as its owner (restructure, 'one algebraic completion owner and one category-O consumer'), which has no design job yet. Until it exists these statements are imported as this contract; no node of this roadmap plans them. Also supply the restricted BGG dual associated to a root-reversing anti-involution fixing the Cartan, with exactness, involutivity and preservation of simple highest-weight modules (BR15 pp. 14–15). This dual is distinct from the ordinary contragredient.

gaps.title: Proof of Dospinescu–Le Bras, Lemme 5.10

After passage to seminormed quotients, the missing input is the nonarchimedean Schur property for normed spaces. The existing compactoid supplier does not by itself show that the weakly compact sequence together with 0 is compactoid. Supply a complete proof or a cleared, exact published locator; the earlier suggested compactoid argument is withdrawn. No uncleared book was read.

BR16 Corollary 2.5 proves the first socle; it does not by itself supply the second. This is an open proof contract, not a claimed general full-faithfulness extension.
